items.body: Palagoma is not only the first release from Nairobi-based label Cool Waters, it also marks the first time German-born, Kenya-based percussionist Sven Kacirek has collaborated with Ogoya Nengo and Olith Ratengo at the same time. Odd Okoddo, the duo of Kacirek and Ratengo, has been performing since 2018, but with the inclusion of the 83 year old Nengo, a singer from the eastern part of the country, there�s an added traditional depth to the music. A 2025 performance shows Nengo�s lifetime of experience singing Kenya�s dodo tradition around 2 and half minutes in (see below). Furthermore, her inclusion on this album allows her and Ratengo to toss the vocals back and forth as they reference their shared roots (Ratengo and Nengo live minutes from each other). Musically, however, the tracks are driven by Kacirek�s Buchla synth, hand percussion, and occasional kit drumming, which serve to buoy the voices without blotting out the music�s origins. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Bara,� for example, begins with the dime-store thwack of a repeated pattern, a stiff juxtaposition to the voices; yet, as the song rolls along, a 4/4 clink appears, then a burbling bass, and finally, what sounds like a xylophone. Layers of synthesized polyrhythms keep presenting themselves with a subtlety almost unnoticeable, until, by the track�s end, it feels organic, as if it�s all been underneath the two voices all along. Palagoma by Odd Okoddo & Ogoya Nengo �Sarah,� perhaps the album�s most intense track, features a lead vocal from Ratengo and tentative, percussive spittles from Kacirek. And while the technology never tries to overtake the vocals, it does sneak up and punctuate the track�s urgency, as edgy distortion sneaks in here and there just as Ratengo�s voice reaches its peak. The term �folktronica� has been bandied about as a way to house the type of music on offer here. In fact, exploratory collaborations such as Chouk Bwa & The �ngstr�mers as well as much of Kampala, Uganda�s Nyege Nyege label house sounds that might be �folktronic� in some way. What�s more interesting and important about this music, though, is how truly global so much of it is while maintaining a deep connection to Africa and its diasporic communities. The music on Palagoma , as well as much of what�s linked above (and available in countless other recent recordings) demonstrates a real willingness for cultures to respond to each other without trampling traditions altogether. Instead, roots become avant-garde and innovations become seemingly thousands of years old. Certainly the inclusion of an 83 year old traditional Kenyan singer only recently making her global debut as she tours with a duo whose instrumental voice is a white male saturated in electronic Kenyan rhythms demonstrates this blurring. The music this trio makes is certainly of the 21st century, but it�s often hazy, sparse, and open, keeping it from a quick sell-by date or confining it to a specific genre. Instead, it�s a beautiful example music as grace.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是内罗毕新厂牌Cool Waters的首发作品，由德国出生、肯尼亚定居的打击乐手Sven Kacirek与Olith Ratengo组成的二人组Odd Okoddo，邀请83岁的肯尼亚东部传统dodo歌唱家Ogoya Nengo共同录制。Kacirek以Buchla合成器、手鼓和架子鼓构建电子节拍层，与两位歌手的人声交织，既不掩盖传统根基，又通过层叠的合成复合节奏营造出有机生长的质感。专辑中曲目逐步展开复杂层次，从简朴的打击模式逐渐浮现出4/4节拍、低音和木琴音色，使前卫电子手法与传统人声形成无缝融合。乐评指出这类跨文化合作展现了21世纪音乐的趋势：全球文化交流中根源音乐变得前卫，前卫创新看似古老。这种模糊界限的尝试使传统在全球语境中获得新的表达。

items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.

items._cn_summary: 这张《Songs of Compassion》是Dorothy Moskowitz（前The United States of America成员）与意大利作曲家Francesco Paolo Paladino及诗人Luca Chino Ferrari的合作专辑，包含十一首作品。音乐以钢琴为核心，辅以弦乐、木管、合成器织体与金属质感音色，打破传统功能和声逻辑，强调调式与非线性展开，近似Steve Reich与Philip Glass的简约重复美学。Moskowitz的演唱被形容为方法派演员式的诠释，旋律随意识流起伏，关注每个词的重量。歌词兼具政治批判与哲学沉思：《Pale Wanderer》剖析威权主义的共谋机制，《Charlottesville》（与已故Joe Byrd合写）以抗议诗歌传统回应当下极右浪潮，其余篇章则探讨死亡与宇宙中的位置。整体融合了1960年代实验摇滚的余韵与当代欧洲前卫作曲传统，在地下厂牌Silentes发行。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这支乐队最突出的特征是自制乐器：所有演奏设备均由废弃物、零碎物件拼装而成，包括以坚果、厨房用品命名的各类打击与吹奏装置。在现代录音麦克风的严格捕捉下，这些非常规乐器展现出惊人的音准与丰富音质，乐评对此印象深刻。专辑将自制乐器与多元文化音乐风格深度匹配：开场曲采用单簧管领奏的克莱兹默风格，伴以巴松管低音与急促打击乐；后续曲目分别融入昆比亚、非洲节拍、桑巴及中东旋律元素，各曲中均包含展示演奏者技巧的即兴段落。整张专辑在欢快氛围中探索不同文化组织音乐的方式，同时以废物成器的实践反思音乐的本质——乐手总能找到发声的方法。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items.body: Dreams may be among the strangest territories available to us. Each night, the mind constructs worlds without asking permission from physics, geography, biography, or common sense. We meet people who never existed, return to places that vanished years ago, fall in love with strangers, lose ourselves, recover ourselves, and wake carrying the emotional residue of events that never occurred. There is something almost miraculous in this private universe, because within it we are briefly released from the limits imposed by circumstance. Thought offers a similar freedom. We can imagine nearly anything, even when reality permits us to accomplish only a fraction of it. For Venus Volcanism, the Iceland-based project of Crete-born vocalist, musician, and producer Rena Rasouli, dreams become both refuge and research subject. Her new song, “Dreams,” inhabits the uncertain region between waking life and the private worlds that continue behind our eyes. Rasouli created the song exactly one year ago as the first snow settled across the peaks surrounding Siglufjörður, Iceland’s northernmost town. She keeps a journal beside her bed, recording complete dreams when possible and preserving stray images when that is all sleep leaves behind. Before sleeping, she gives herself a small invocation: “As I close my eyelids and sleep takes me, gently or not, please show me something that will help me understand myself a little better.” Dreams drifts somewhere between dark pop, ambient composition, experimental electronics, and neoclassical music, with affinities to This Mortal Coil, Julee Cruise, Penelope Trappes, and Zola Jesus. Rasouli’s voice occupies the center while drones, synthesizers, arpeggiated figures, and suspended textures create an unstable sense of location. Beauty and unease coexist. The song seems to hover between desire imagined and desire remembered. Its love story belongs to an imaginary lover, though imagination hardly makes the emotion less consequential. Desperation, longing, idealization, and obsession can become perfectly real experiences even when their object remains beyond reach. “Have you ever found yourself dreaming with your eyes open? I honestly don’t know how many times I have done it while diving into Icelandic pools,” says Rasouli. “Especially during winter, I feel like I am balancing somewhere between the conscious and the unconscious, and sometimes I don’t even know how the day has passed. I am and I am not. I exist and I do not exist. I do everything I am supposed to do; I move through the day as I should, but if you know me well enough, you might see it in my eyes: I am somewhere in between.” This suspended condition also governs the video, directed by Tassos Gkoletsos with help from friends and members of the Siglufjörður community. Northern Iceland’s long winter darkness turns ordinary routines into strange repetitions: tending plants, bathing, working, exercising, moving through familiar rooms while another existence unfolds internally. “During those months, I always find myself somewhere in between,” Rasouli continues. “I do everything I need to do and I’m relatively functional, but everything feels like autopilot. At the same time, another scene is taking place inside my head. I dream and imagine other things while going through the ordinary routines of everyday life, like watering my plants, having my bath, working, and going to the gym.” Perhaps this is why Dreams feels so intimate. Rasouli treats imagination as a parallel dimension of daily existence, one without measurable coordinates yet capable of altering everything that happens after we return. items.body: Lift the veil, see what I’ve become An exoskeletal pantheon Born again from bone and breath To spread the living gospel of death On Tears for the Dying‘s blistering new gothic track Devour Me, Adria Stembridge drags the band back toward its earlier roots with a slower, heavier gait, then breaks that crawl apart with abrupt tempo changes that make the song feel unstable beneath your feet. Stembridge handles drum machine, guitar, bass, and vocals, building the track from dark guitar figures, blunt low-end pressure, and drums that move with the patience of something following you home. Her vocals hang above it all in a cold echo, less concerned with theatrical grandstanding than with letting the words rot in the air for a second before the next image lands. You can hear Bauhaus in the skeletal guitar work, Alien Sex Fiend in the queasy theatricality, and PiL and Fields of the Nephilim in the sense that somebody has wandered far enough from civilization to start inventing a religion. That religious impulse becomes central once the lyrics start opening the trapdoor. Stembridge draws from cosmic horror, but the terror here feels brutally physical. A solitary figure encounters an impossible swarm, loses control of the body piece by piece, and becomes host to something that treats flesh as raw material. Bones break. Insects burrow. The victim survives only in the technical sense, gradually becoming an alien deity whose transformation has erased whatever person existed before. The nastiest idea arrives afterward: worship. What begins as predation becomes conversion, and the ruined body becomes scripture. Consumption, reproduction, faith, and extermination collapse together until divinity itself starts looking like another parasitic infection. There is something wonderfully foul about that conception of godhood, especially coming from a band whose Southern gothic deathrock has long carried radical queer politics alongside its horror imagery. Authority here comes crawling out of meat. The slower passages give those images room to breathe before the faster sections shove everything toward panic. That contrast is crucial. Speed alone would turn the song into pursuit; the deliberate sections make you wait for whatever is chewing through the floorboards. By the final transformation, cosmic horror has lost every trace of abstraction. Infinity sprouts mandibles, theology breeds larvae, and salvation becomes a forced rebirth inside a body that has been converted into temple, nursery, and weapon. Listen to Devour Me below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: 这张单曲由Stembridge独立操刀鼓机、吉他、贝斯与人声，以黑暗吉他动机、厚重的低频和缓慢推进的节奏构建整体氛围。歌曲在沉重缓慢的段落与突然的节奏断裂间切换，制造出一种不稳定感。人声悬于器乐之上，以冷冽回响呈现，刻意避免戏剧化，让歌词意象在空气中缓慢腐朽。歌词取材于宇宙恐怖，但将恐惧落实于肉身：孤独个体遭遇无法抵抗的虫群，身体被逐步侵蚀、改造，最终成为异质神祇的宿主。吞噬、繁殖、信仰与灭绝在此坍缩为一体，神性被重新定义为寄生性的感染。乐评指出作品延续了南方哥特死亡摇滚的美学传统，同时承载着激进的酷儿政治表达，将宗教冲动转化为对权力与肉身的关系审视。

items.body: The screams of children, far away Echo in this perfect day A perfect society becomes considerably harder to admire once somebody explains who has been paying for it. In Ursula K. Le Guin’s The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas, an entire city’s happiness depends upon the suffering of a single child, an arrangement its citizens learn to accept as the price of their good fortune. There is plenty of room for horror in that cheerful consensus, especially once the people benefiting from it begin explaining why things simply have to be this way. Bologna’s La Mano Sinistra, whose name means “the left hand” in Italian, take up that ugly bargain on their debut single, Unnecessary Perfection. The track introduces Omelas, a seven-track concept album due November 6, 2026, through Bat-Cave Productions, translating Le Guin’s ethical dilemma into gothic rock with enough melodic momentum to carry its uncomfortable questions straight onto the dancefloor. A heartbeat rhythm opens the track, its alternating accents pressing against sustained, cold synthesizer tones before a thick, low-slung bassline sends everything forward. Guitar and electronics give the melody a generous sweep while Davide Sacco sings with the decadent authority of a frontman who can make a warning sound almost inviting. The combination brings to mind The Danse Society around their Heaven Is Waiting era, with something of Children on Stun and Brotherhood of Pagans in the vocal delivery and the way the instruments lock together. The guitar break ascends and descends through the melody, supplying an exhilarating lift while sustaining the chill of the surrounding synths. When Sacco’s voice returns alongside it, a more romantic quality enters his timbre, adding a strange tenderness to the accusation. This is the kind of gothic rock that makes getting dressed to go out feel like the opening scene of an evening full of possibilities. For a song about the moral cost of everybody having a good time, it has a wicked talent for getting the evening started. The lyrics initially survey a population blessed with sharp minds, untouched lives, and the promise of a cure for all, while concealed currents move beneath that reassuring surface. Sacco’s recurring question, “What’s necessary, what is not,” unsettles the supposed inevitability of the arrangement. By the closing lines, children’s screams carry across the distance into the perfect day itself. Read alongside Le Guin’s story, that distance becomes part of the accusation: comfort depends upon keeping suffering far enough away to be tolerated, even when its beneficiaries know exactly what sustains their happiness. The band describe the single this way: “The paradox of perfection. A fast-paced, impactful track reflecting the fictitious tranquility of a society built upon the distant screams of the weakest.” The accompanying video gives that selective vision an effective visual counterpart. High-contrast black-and-white performance footage is crossed by horizontal bands that repeatedly interrupt faces, instruments, and the lyrics appearing on screen. Close-ups of hands working the strings alternate with Sacco at the microphone, while the bars make even the plainest words momentarily difficult to see. The treatment suggests an uncomfortable connection between an obstructed image and a society accustomed to accepting a partial view. Watch the video for Unnecessary Perfection below: La Mano Sinistra brings together Sacco on vocals and lyrics, Gianluca Lo Presti of Nevica on bass and electronics, and Giuseppe Lo Bue of Caron Dimonio on guitar and electronics. Sacco is also a co-founder of the contemporary theatre company ErosAntEros and artistic director of POLIS Teatro Festival, a background that gives the project’s theatrical character a clear foundation. Omelas grew out of Sacco’s stage production of The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas, performed by actress Eva Robin’s. Recorded at Loto Studio in Ravenna during the summer of 2025, the album develops its source material across seven chapters, addressing indifference, collective guilt, and the decision to abandon a prosperity built upon injustice for an uncertain life beyond it. Unnecessary Perfection is available on digital platforms. Omelas follows on November 6, 2026, via Bat-Cave Productions. items._cn_summary: 意大利波洛尼亚三人组合以Le Guin的经典短篇为蓝本，构建了一张关于道德困境的概念专辑。这首首发单曲以心跳节奏、冷调合成器与低沉贝斯线开场，吉他与合成器交织出宽阔的旋律走向，人声呈现出颓废而具权威感的质感，带有80年代英国哥特摇滚的影子。歌词层面，歌曲审视一个看似完美的社会如何将弱势者的苦难推到视野之外，反复诘问'什么是必要的，什么不是'，将舒适与共谋的关系推至前台。黑白高对比度的MV强化了这层视觉批判。整体制作在类型框架内展现出概念深度与旋律张力，适合暗潮场景下兼具思辨与舞动需求的听众。

items.tags: クラシック 現代音楽 intoxicate 2026 August クラシック 現代音楽 # リイシュー クラシック 里見暁美 松平頼暁
items.excerpt: 『ピアノ・ホライズン』に80年代の日本の音楽シーンを垣間見る。ローズからモールス信号のような単音の連打が聴こえ、クラヴィのクラスターが連打を断ち切る。ファンキーな音色にマイルス・デイヴィスの音楽のようだと感じるが、リズムにグルーヴが感じられるわけではない。松平頼暁がこのアルバムを企画したピアニスト里見暁美に書き下ろした“エリクサトーン”だ。しばらくしてピアノが緩やかに辿る下降音形が聴こえ、そこに時折りピアノからの異音が混じり、雨後のアスファルトから昇る蒸気のような音場が立ち上がる。藤枝守の“フォーリング・スケール第6番”だ。この二人の作品は〈表現内容よりも構造が強調〉されていると近藤譲はノートに記す。

items._cn_summary: 这张1981年的专辑由里见晓美演奏两位作曲家松平赖晓与藤枝守的钢琴作品。松平赖晓的《Elixir-tone》以单音连打模拟莫尔斯电码，簇音打断节奏，音色funky却不具groove，呈现近似Miles Davis的质感。藤枝守的《Falling Scale No.6》以缓慢下行的音形与偶发的钢琴异音构建声场，如雨后沥青升起的蒸汽。近藤让在笔记中指出，二人作品皆强调结构优先于表现内容。专辑呈现80年代日本当代古典创作中结构主义与实验语汇的交汇点，对先锋钢琴音乐爱好者具有研究价值。

items._cn_summary: 本文是对《Good Experimental Music》2026年9月期合辑的综述，由Marc Masters主笔，共涵盖二十张新发行专辑，其中十张附有详细评论，另十张仅作推荐。所涉及作品横跨drone、即兴、电子与声音艺术四大领域，代表性作品包括Cinchel的《The 4 Stages of Long Phase》、Brittany Karlson与Nick Neuburg合作的《Duo: Vol. 1》、Leafcutter John的《Warm Grit》以及Rob Magill的《Subtle Chaos》。整张合辑呈现了实验音乐在音色探索与结构处理上的多样性，从长时段相位偏移到暖质颗粒合成，再到即兴对话与微声混沌，均体现出创作者对声音物质性的持续关注。该综述为听众提供了一份较为全面的当代实验音乐月度索引，适合作为风格探索的入口参考。

items.body: Curbside Lambsear Put Rings On All My Fingers To Weigh Down My Hands Members of The Umlauts and caroline find scrappy joy in dissonant chaos mixed with cinematic grandeur Put Rings On All My Fingers To Weigh Down My Hands by Curbside Lambsear This is an intriguingly hard-to-pin-down debut from London’s Curbside Lambsear, AKA Magdalena McLean and Annabelle Mödlinger. Having met while playing in the (still active) art punk band The Umlauts, the duo assembled this lengthy EP in a patchwork fashion. You wouldn't know it. There’s a coherent sense of purpose to these five tracks, as well as a free-roaming attitude when it comes to genre. The post punk-tinged opener, ‘No Ordinary Word’, slouches in on heavy-limbed drums and thick, dubby bass, Mödlinger's insouciant vocals... items._cn_summary: 这是伦敦二人组Curbside Lambsear的首张EP式专辑，由The Umlauts乐队的Magdalena McLean与Annabelle Mödlinger组建。两人以拼贴方式制作了这张包含五首曲目的作品，却呈现出统一的创作意图与跨类型自由探索的态度。开场曲以厚重的鼓击与浑浊的低频贝斯为基底，配合松弛随性的演唱，营造出后朋克的不羁气息。整体风格在失调混乱与电影化的宏大感之间游走，展现出实验性的声响美学。两位成员来自艺术朋克乐队The Umlauts及caroline的创作背景，为这张作品注入了独立地下音乐的鲜活基因与即兴式的不拘一格。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Apparently Jazz-Rock Fusion guitarist Volker Kriegel was paying close attention to the sudden rise of Power Fusion "super groups" popping up around the Jazz-Rock Fusion world (including Tony Williams' Lifetime, Jack DeJohnette's Complex, Chris Hinze's Combination, Klaus Doldinger's Passport, Brian Auger's Oblivion Express, John McLaughlin's Mahavishnu Orchestra, Chick Corea's Return To Forever, Joe Zawinul's Weather Report, Michal Urbaniak's Fusion, Herbie Hancock's Headhunters, Clive Stevens' Atmospheres, Larry Coryell's Eleventh House, and, soon to come, Todd Rundgren's Utopia, Larry Young's Fuel, Tom Scott's L.A. Express, Jack DeJohnette's Direction(s), John Abercrombie's Gateway, and Stomu Yamash'ta's Go) for he decided to tag the "Spectrum" label onto this album project to connote and honor the foursome of exceptional collaborators he found to help him achieve the high standards of musicianship necessary to pull off his increasingly complex and demanding compositions. This collection of Volker Kriegel original compositions was recorded and mixed at Studio Waldorf in Frankfurt, Deutschland, between February 18 and 23, 1974, and then released by MPS Records sometime in 1974. Knowing MPS' recording-to-release turn-around patterns from the era (as well as Volker Kriegel's status as a recognized and established recording artist), I think it safe to estimate that Mild Maniac would likely have been released in the Spring of 1974.A1. "Mindwill" (6:45) some super-funky bass is joined/doubled by a second deep-funky bass, stinky funk drumming and low volume guitar, keys, and percussion as the song opens and the motif establishes itself. Effected guitar and super-funky electric piano move forward as a three-note vocal-like melody line seems to loop (which turns out to come from Eberhard's cello!), forming the blood to the rhythm section's backbone as Rainer Br�ninghaus' keys and Volker's guitar (and, later, Eberhard's bass & cello) flit and fly around the sonosphere on this amazingly-well engineered song. So cool! (14.25/15)A2. "Prinz Eisenherz" (4:37) this one opens up with some ECM-like pristine sound rendering of double bass, acoustic guitar, multiple keyboards, and subtle percussion noises putting together a gentle yet full and subtly-nuanced motif. This interestingly-nuanced Mahavishnu-like whole group play continues throughout the song, start to finish, without the tempo ever clicking into gear (and never admitting Joe Nay's drums), just kind of floating on the top of the stream the whole way. Interesting! Amazing sonic clarity! It feels as if I can pick up every sound of each musician's hand movements. (8.875/10) A3. "Schnellh�rspiel" (5:26) Billy Cobham-like drums and Jan Hammer-like keyboard work open this high speed song as Eberhard and Volker add barks, yelps, and yowls from their own instruments as the music congeals into a Herbie Headhunter/Mahavishnu 2.0 train ride through the forests of Southern Germany. The technically-demanding high-speed multiple-instrument phrases are so like those pioneered by Chick Corea's Return To Forever's Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy and The Mahavishnu Orchestra's Birds of Fire (both 1973 releases) that it's amazing to hear them so soon coming from an European band. (Material like this and other elements of this album also remind me greatly of Todd Rundgren's own response to the Power Fusion phenomenon: his October release of the Todd Rundgren's Utopia album). Very impressive musicianship and sound production. (9.25/10)A4. "Mild Maniac" (5:08) a little smoother, a little more laid back, just as erudite and virtuosic despite the use of acoustic guitars, bowed cello and bass, gentle electric piano, and easier-on-the-brain melodies. These musicians are just so darn impressive! (9/10) B1. "The Visit" (7:26) loose though timed spaces in which all five musicians are freed to explore and express melodic lines and rhythms are punctuated by intermittent chord-and-drum punches as Volker and Rainer eventually "strike up a bargain" of flow and chord-commitment to which Joe, Peter, and Eberhard ascribe, resulting in the evolution in the third minute to a quirky little hook motif that sounds like a funky theme song to a television show (as was a fairly common phenomenon in 1974). By the arrival of the fourth minute that which sounded so quaint and almost trite (and yet expresses a Herbie Hancock-like level of sophistication and demand placed upon the musicians on hand) has evolved even further into something more akin to super funky Jan Hammer/George Duke song. Eberhard Weber and Joe Nay are simply phenomenal, as is Volker: shredding mercilessly away with his saw-like electric guitar tone until 6:50 when everything stops, leaving a steel-stringed acoustic guitar to finish things off before someone can be heard stomping across the floorboards on his exit from the recording room. Great stuff! (13.5/15)B2. "D-D�del" (12:12) dirty electric piano playing solo for the first two minutes of this before the rest of the band joins in with a BOB JAMES-like jazz-lite rendition of THE MARSHALL TUCKER BAND's 1973 hit song, "Can't You See" until the end of the fifth minute when everything devolves into a spacey, "Also Sprach Zarathustra" intro-like jazz atmosphere for Eberhard to have one of his "underwater" solos (this could be the first one I've heard of the sort that would become his trademark style and sound in a year or two). Eberhard eventually gathers steam: working his way into what becomes a very impressive display of full-fledged bass virtuosity--which the rest of the band responds to by joining in, each in turn exhibiting their own wildly-imaginative improvisations into the free jazz mix until the clock spring seems to reach its end, everything slowing down like the end of an Ever-Redi battery's charge to some children's toy. The end! Cool and eminently impressive! What a ride! Like a rollercoaster moving inside a slightly-disturbing amusement park funhouse. (22.625/25)Total time: 41:34A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of eclectic but time-sensitive Third Wave Jazz-Rock Fusion that at times rivals some of the era's elite Power Fusion band outputs.
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年专辑由德国爵士摇滚吉他手Volker Kriegel领衔，以"Spectrum"为概念召集四位乐手组建超级组合，在法兰克福Studio Waldorf完成录制。作品中融合了Mahavishnu Orchestra式的复杂整体演奏、Headhunters式的放克律动以及ECM式的精致声学质感。开篇曲目以双贝斯叠加与电子键盘构建深沉放克骨架，大提琴音色与人声化旋律线交织；中段曲目在纯静音色中漂浮，整体克制而不失层次；后续曲目则转向高速奔涌，键盘与鼓组呼应Cobham与Hammer的风格。录音工程水准极高，演奏细节纤毫毕现。MPS厂牌虽具一定商业属性，但在爵士领域以独立精神著称。该专辑属于70年代欧洲爵士摇滚融合场景中对美式Power Fusion潮流的德语回应，兼具技术复杂度与音色探索意识。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — It must have been so exciting for a music fan of that era because all sorts of stuff were coming out. Soft Machine were pioneers really, being one of the most influential psychedelic/progressive acts of their time. This album, their debut, the only with Kevin Ayers on, is so exciting because of the top notch musicianship despite being difficult to follow on some parts. Really amazing blend of jazz/rock/pop that keeps you interested along the way.Really groovy rhythm section with Kevin Ayers on bass and Robert Wyatt on drums who is also doing the vocals. Mike Ratledge on organ on the other hand, like his British peers on that time, is truly mesmerizing.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / progressive / jazz-rock / Canterbury scene
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Soft Machine的首张作品，也是唯一一张有Kevin Ayers参与录制的专辑。作为坎特伯雷乐派的先驱，乐队将爵士、摇滚与流行元素进行了大胆融合，音乐技术上表现出色，尽管部分段落较为复杂难懂。Kevin Ayers的低音与Robert Wyatt的鼓点和演唱构成了紧凑而富有律动的节奏骨架，Mike Ratledge的风琴演奏在当时英国乐手群体中显得尤为出色。整张专辑节奏感突出，器乐之间的对话展现出那个时代音乐探索的前沿精神，将迷幻氛围与爵士即兴结构相结合，为后来前卫摇滚的发展奠定了基础。

items.body: “Dancing has its time, mourning has its time”, runs a line in “Gamachume”, the new single from Tbilisi artists Tamada and DillaNext, and a Georgian supra works exactly that way. The supra is the country’s traditional banquet, a long table of food and wine presided over by the tamada, who holds the room and proposes toast after toast, to peace, to family, to the homeland and to the dead. The guests drink after each one and often break into song. Singer and producer Lasha Chkhapelia named himself Tamada after that role, and across Dionysus vs Tamada and 2024’s 9 Deadly Sins for Tamada he has written his lyrics as toasts in ancient Georgian and set them over electronic beats. This time the glass is raised to Sukhumi, the main city of Abkhazia, a Georgian region on the Black Sea. Abkhaz separatist forces, backed by Russia, seized the region in the 1992–93 war, and most of the world still recognises it as part of Georgia. Chkhapelia and Zura Jishkariani, the novelist and poet who records as DillaNext, were among around 250,000 Georgians driven out as children. The lyric pictures a boy with a pistol and a rose, with Black Sea currents running down through his genes. The pair used the same image on last year’s “Sokhumeli Bichi” (“Sukhumian Boy”), where the sea ran through the veins of the boy of the title. In both songs the city passes down by blood, from parents who lived there to children who left too young to remember it. Another verse turns a burial into a planting: others dig the earth, he is the one laid in it, and the people who took him for dead find they have planted a tree of life. Thirty-three years after the war emptied Sukhumi of its Georgians, two of the children it drove out are putting the city into songs made in Tbilisi, and that is the tree the verse describes. “Gamachume” arrived with a video on 27 September on Deep Douqan, the label behind Tamada’s most recent singles. It closes on its title, Georgian for “silence me”, five times over, sung by the same voice that earlier claims it can “break armies apart”. At a supra, the tamada decides when the room falls quiet. items._cn_summary: 这首作品来自格鲁吉亚第比利斯的两位艺术家Tamada与DillaNext，以电子节拍承载古格鲁吉亚语歌词，将传统的祝酒词形式与现代制作融合。歌词主题围绕苏呼米——这座在1992-93年战争中被分离主义力量夺走的黑海城市，作者本人即是被驱逐的约25万格鲁吉亚人中的儿童。文本将埋葬转化为种树，暗示离散的族群记忆如何在新土壤中生根，呈现出深沉的政治与文化乡愁。重复的'沉默我'结尾与传统宴饮中tamada主导节奏的仪式感相呼应。作品由独立厂牌Deep Douqan发行，结合地理边缘性、离散叙事与电子民谣实验，是一首在文化记忆层面极具分量的跨域作品。

items.body: CATASTROFE CLUB have reached the point where the extinction of humanity begins to sound suspiciously like good news. On Un Dia Mejor, Josep M. Herrera and David Molina survey civilization’s wreckage with the composure of two men who have already accepted that we’ve been hurtling toward disaster since about WW1. The Granollers duo’s fourth single previews UN FUTURO TRANQUILO, their fourth album, due this October through Periphylla Records. Following the trilogy that defined their earlier work, the record opens another chapter for a project whose interests have always stretched far beyond any useful genre designation. Post-punk, darkwave, electronics, post-rock and pop all pass through the machinery, with Herrera’s rough spoken delivery sitting somewhere between public announcement, philosophical complaint and the guy at the end of the bar who has finally assembled enough evidence to prove civilization was a clerical error. Un Dia Mejor begins amid catastrophe. Lights die, people run through darkness, civilization appears to reach its conclusion, and somehow the central idea remains stubbornly hopeful. The song imagines collapse as an opening rather than merely an endpoint, asking why humanity remains frightened of change, love and the possibility of an existence radically different from the one it has built for itself. CATASTROFE CLUB can stare directly at environmental ruin, social collapse and human stupidity while maintaining an odd serenity, as though extinction might finally allow every other creature on Earth a decent night’s sleep. Musically, the group pushes further into post-rock scale and cinematic space while keeping their electronic foundation intact. Layers accumulate gradually around bass, keyboards, guitars and programming, giving the track a broad horizon without losing the dry, severe personality that has followed Herrera and Molina throughout their catalogue. Their stated influences include Sigur Rós, Idles, Fontaines D.C., Astrud and Los Punsetes, though those reference points function more like distant road signs than destinations. The accompanying video extends the song’s worldview through a montage of retrofuturist imagery, historical disorder, and footage of the duo performing. Visions of technological progress collide with reminders of twentieth-century chaos, creating the uncomfortable sensation of watching humanity repeatedly advertise tomorrow while wrecking today. Watch the video for Un dia mejor below: Tension sits at the center of UN FUTURO TRANQUILO. CATASTROFE CLUB imagines a peaceful future precisely because humanity may no longer occupy it. There is cruelty in the joke, certainly, but also a strange tenderness toward whatever survives us. For these two chroniclers of decline, a better day may still be coming. We simply might not be invited. items._cn_summary: 西班牙二人组CATASTROFE CLUB的第四张专辑延续其对文明衰落的冷峻观察。这张作品将后朋克、暗潮、合成器电子与后摇滚的宽广音景融为一体，赫雷拉粗粝的念白贯穿于低音、键盘、吉他与编程之间，像公共通告与哲学控诉的混合体。单曲以末日场景开场，却将崩溃视为新的开端而非终点。编曲上层层叠加，逐步拓展出电影化的空间感，同时保持干燥而严厉的气质。音乐影响横跨Sigur Rós至Idles等多种风格，但仅作为远方的路标而非终点。整张专辑的核心理念在于：平静的未来或许正因人类不在场才能实现，其中既有残酷的黑色幽默，也流露出对幸存者的温柔。

items.body: I gave myself the power of keeping you away Wrapped up in the sounds of the bastion’s coldest waves I still see you watching me move towards the within Frankie Diez seems to have reached the useful stage in an artist’s life where embarrassment stops being a factor. Casual Confrontation began on indie-pop ground, but after five albums since 2020, Diez has clearly decided there are worse things than making the music you actually wanted to hear when you were younger, hanging around punk and goth scenes, absorbing whatever seeped in through the walls. “I’ve always been inspired and involved within the punk, goth, and alternative subcultures, and it’s about time my music began reflecting that,” says Diez. You can hear that decision all over SCARED OF SILENCE, the second single from Casual Confrontation’s forthcoming album BASTION. Moving deeper into darkwave and coldwave, Diez has hit upon a combination that feels absurdly overdue: reggaeton and those colder electronic forms sound like tenants who have spent years banging on opposite sides of the same wall, only to discover they were keeping time together. The guitars come in with that severe Twin Tribes economy, the bass carries some of Boy Harsher’s nightclub menace, and beneath it sits a rhythm that keeps trying to pull the song somewhere warmer, dirtier, and more physical. Reggaeton reveals repetition as pressure; a dembow rhythm can keep working on you until thought becomes secondary. EBM has spent decades using similar repetition for control, tension, intimidation, and release. Put them together and suddenly the distance between Bad Bunny and Ultra Sunn starts looking much shorter than anyone bothered to admit. By the second half, the resemblance to Karol G and Tokischa becomes harder to miss. The track loosens at the waist while retaining its colder frame, and that friction gives it personality. Ministry once made metallic percussion feel like a municipal requirement; Diez borrows some of that hard impact and drops it into a song that would rather dance than march. He has a name for the approach, too: “Reggaeton Gótico,” which sounds at first like the sort of phrase somebody invents at closing time and then regrets by breakfast. Except the music holds up the joke. Diez explains why with a much simpler answer: “I always listened to reggaeton growing up in both Puerto Rico and in Miami, and the genre fusion always felt natural, since much of reggaeton can easily have somewhat of a dark-clubbing atmosphere already.” Lyrically, SCARED OF SILENCE continues the story begun in the previous single, ARREBATO, carrying the sense of an unsafe outside world into a more private confrontation. Here, safety means shutting out the person who made the world feel threatening and looking inward for somewhere to stand. Meditative yet fierce, the song casts silence as a way to reclaim power from a toxic dynamic, finding a strange pleasure in no longer owing someone access. When an argument reaches a point where even explaining becomes exhausting, Silence becomes the final boundary, and the anger behind it settles into deliberate withdrawal. There is control in choosing when the conversation ends, especially when every earlier exchange has left someone else setting the terms. Diez gives that decision room to breathe, treating solitude as a place where the self can begin to take shape again. One lyric extends that idea across BASTION as a whole: “When the outside space no longer feels safe, I’ll leave here to see what my heart creates.” The line supplies the forthcoming album BASTION’s central premise, with retreat becoming an opportunity to make something from whatever remains beyond another person’s reach. By the end, the recurring question about silence has changed shape. It sounds almost taunting now, as if Diez already knows the answer and has finally stopped caring whether the other person admits it. items._cn_summary: Casual Confrontation 主创 Frankie Diez 在第五张专辑中将自身成长于波多黎各和迈阿密所吸收的雷鬼动与近年深耕的暗潮冷潮电子并置，提出"哥特雷鬼动"这一概念。评论指出两者共享重复律动作为压力与控制的机制，使这首作品在暗色调合成器与低音线条之上叠入 dembow 节拍，产生既可舞动又具威胁感的张力。编曲层面参考了 Twin Tribes 的经济感吉他、Boy Harsher 的夜店压迫感以及 Ministry 的硬质打击乐，整体框架偏冷却带拉丁律动的体温。歌词层面延续前作主题，将沉默视为从有害关系中夺回自主权的途径，冥想与攻击性交织。文章以具体音乐分析支撑论点，兼具文化背景说明与制作细节观察。

items.body: Halcyon eyes, kind of gloomy in-between (If not now, then when we gonna do it, baby?) Holy pledge, Nostradamus said we’re clean (If not you, then who is gonna teach it to me?) PONS have somehow made a song that sounds as though a demon discovered stimulants, bought an expensive string section, read half a book about Roman emperors, and immediately decided he ought to run for king of hell. IF NOT NOW… is five-plus minutes of Brooklyn dance-punk delirium built around repetition as both engine and psychological hazard. Jack Parker and company plant a krautrock riff in the floorboards, then proceed to furnish the room with strings, horns, electronic abrasion, post-punk angles, and enough manic forward motion to make stopping seem medically inadvisable. Somewhere between Suicide, Brainiac, Liars, Sextile, and Ecce Schnak, after several catastrophic decisions, PONS turn excess into an organizing principle. Parker admits that excess comes naturally. “I have a really maximalist impulse when I’m writing music that I’ve recently been trying to get away from.” You can hear him losing that argument in spectacular fashion. The Eclectica String Quartet enters the picture alongside arrangements refined with Steve La Rosa, and suddenly the song has the air of an espionage film whose secret agent has misplaced the microfilm and joined a Dionysian cult instead. The repetition is crucial. PONS keep worrying the central figure until familiarity starts producing strange side effects, with each return carrying another detail, another escalation, another reason to suspect somebody has slipped something questionable into the punch. Parker wanted “something as repetitive and hypnotic as possible,” and the band stretches that idea toward absurdity without losing its grip on the dance floor. Lyrically, appetite keeps mutating. Sex, ambition, prophecy, intoxication, history, conquest, divine entitlement, and cultural memory pile together until the speaker begins sounding less like a romantic opportunist than somebody preparing to annex a small republic before breakfast. Desire becomes destiny; destiny develops an ego problem. By the closing stretch, bravery, brutality, providence, and personal mythology have become indistinguishable enough to suggest that civilization may have been a clerical error. Animator Arturo Baston pushes the same madness into the accompanying video. “Arturo had the idea of animating some sort of nightmare carnival bumper car ride filled with freaks and ghouls,” says Parker. From there, Parker becomes a Ghost Rider-like figure traveling through the underworld on his way toward infernal royalty, because apparently ordinary professional advancement was unavailable. Watch the video for If NOT NOW… below: IF NOT NOW… belongs to the forthcoming RACECAR, out November 5 via Casa Gogol Records, Eugene Hütz’s new label. If this single represents the album’s governing philosophy, PONS have built themselves a machine whose accelerator has been welded permanently to the floor. Normies should probably stand clear. items._cn_summary: PONS的单曲以重复为结构引擎，将克拉特摇滚riff、弦乐四重奏、铜管、电子噪音与后朋克棱角熔于一炉，打造出五分多钟的舞蹈-朋克狂热。乐队自称有极简主义冲动，却在这首歌中彻底败给自身的极繁主义，将过剩转化为组织原则。歌词围绕野心、欲望、预言与征服层层堆叠，主题从情欲逐渐滑向帝国式扩张与神话自诮。重复段落被反复打磨，每次回归都加入新细节，制造出催眠式的心理张力。配乐由Ecce Schnak风格的弦乐四重奏与编曲共同构建，带有邪典电影配气质。MV中主唱化身地狱骑士穿行于怪物嘉年华，延续了音频中的混乱意象。整张专辑将于11月通过Casa Gogol Records发行，这是Gogol Bordello主脑Eugene Hütz创立的新厂牌。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，汇集三支乐队——弦乐四重奏Spectrum Quartett、传统民间小提琴组合Nogaband及女声合唱团Ulijanky——重新演绎斯洛伐克作曲家Eugen Suchoň、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes及匈牙利作曲家Béla Bartók取材于乡村音乐的作品。演奏者们深入民间传统采风，使古典作品重新回归其源头活水。专辑并非管弦乐式的平滑处理，而是充满原始能量与即兴活力的演奏与演唱。作品将古典作曲技法与民间演奏技巧、声乐传统深度融合，展现了斯洛伐克传统音乐与其古典音乐传统之间持续对话的可能性。对关注世界音乐与跨界融合的听众而言，这是一次兼具学术严谨与泥土气息的聆听体验。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)
items.label: Bongo Joe
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比这两个大西洋小岛在1970至80年代——即非洲所谓黄金时期——录制的Puxa音乐。Puxa是一种节奏与文化大熔炉，融合了来自其他前葡萄牙非洲殖民地的音乐元素以及Merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等加勒比风格，并承载着葡萄牙殖民时期的历史记忆——百年前葡方曾试图禁绝Puxa舞蹈，但显然以失败告终。专辑共收录15首作品，由Pedro Lima领衔的多位艺人参与，呈现多把吉他交织缠绕、主唱与和声彼此呼应的结构，节奏段贝斯与键盘留白时，鼓与吉他接力推进，催动舞者持续数小时狂欢。来自非洲非主流地区的独立小厂牌Bongo Joe发行，地理与文化层面的独特性使这张合辑成为窥探这段鲜被记录的音乐史的重要窗口。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)
items.label: tak:til / Glitterbeat
items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton 的新作《The Gods Laugh》延续了她标志性的模糊边界美学，将民谣、前卫元素与宗教氛围融为一炉。中提琴、簧风琴、锤击扬琴与钢琴构成核心编制，此番加入鼓、贝斯与合成器拓展了音色维度。多首作品以即兴方式一次完成录制，呈现出穿越时空的静谧神秘感。John Clare 的诗作被谱入旋律，漂浮于持续低音之上；中世纪圣咏式的开篇逐渐过渡为钢琴主导的缓慢级进。专辑也是对亡父的纪念之作，特定曲目描绘其最后一次前往钟爱菜园的旅程，渗透出超越言语的温情。光与暗在音乐中相互渗透，情绪流转自如，拒绝被简单归类，是兼具挑战性与感染力的创作。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 挪威Camilla Hole Trio的新专辑在前作科幻合成器与民俗融合的基础上回归更朴素的音色，但探索本土以外民间音乐的意图依然延续。主奏乐器高音萨克斯自带爵士基因，首曲以西挪威传统Springleik舞曲旋律为起点，贝斯手与鼓手以模块合成器和颤音琴叠加色彩。乐队内部角色分配极为模糊，旋律在萨克斯与贝斯之间交接，鼓手不断扩展节奏空间，乐句走向逐渐进入自由即兴领域，尾声处萨克斯再次确认主题旋律。整体呈现出对挪威西海岸民俗材料的解构与重组，将传统舞蹈旋律置于爵士即兴与电子声响的语境中重新审视。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威音乐人组成的三重奏录制，基于斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材进行重新诠释。乐评指出，作品虽源自舞曲旋律，却在演奏方式上更接近室内乐——三位乐手沉浸在亲密的音乐对话中，揭示了北欧舞曲表面欢快下潜藏的暗流。评论特别提到以挪威Setesdal山谷的"Fossgrimen"传说（瀑布精灵被认为赋予小提琴手技艺，因此小提琴被视为魔鬼的乐器）开篇的象征意义。编曲中，传统乐器如sjøfløyte（竖笛）与小提琴、鼓形成层次丰富的对话，音乐在行进中不断碎片化直至瓦解，展现出对传统素材的实验性解构态度。这种处理方式模糊了民间音乐、即兴演奏与室内乐之间的界限。

items.body: Susanne Sundfør Revelations of Divine Love With just her voice and an a pipe organ, the Norwegian singer-songwriterpays tribute to Julian of Norwich Revelations of Divine Love by Susanne Sundfør with Kit Downes Even at her most austere and experimental, Susanne Sundfør has a way of creating amenable and approachable music that is infused with her own brand of idiosyncratic enchantment, and so it is with Revelations of Divine Love. The singer-songwriter’s seventh album is inspired by recent motherhood and a profound connection with the texts of the fourteenth-century English mystic and anchoress Julian of Norwich. Sundfør recorded this album live in an empty but acoustically conducive Norwegian church with just her voice and the accompaniment of a pipe organ. If that configuration sounds... items._cn_summary: 挪威创作歌手苏珊娜·森弗以人声与管风琴为核心，在空旷的挪威教堂中进行现场录制，完成第七张专辑。这张作品的灵感来源于她近年成为母亲的人生经历，以及对十四世纪英国神秘主义者朱利安·诺里奇宗教文本的深层共鸣。整张专辑以极简编制呈现，仅保留人声与管风琴的对话，教堂本身的空间声学成为第三件乐器。作者延续了自身一贯的创作特质，在严谨克制的框架中注入个性化的诗意与精神性维度，将中世纪宗教文本与现代作曲语汇进行融合探索。作品介于当代古典与艺术歌曲之间，结构空灵而内向，适合在安静环境中沉浸聆听，展现了北欧独立音乐人在声音实验与精神性表达上的独特路径。

items.body: Winter Sect have discovered one of goth’s better-kept secrets: graveyards can be funny places. Not funny in the sitcom sense, unless your sitcom happens to involve velvet sleeves, low fog, marble angels, and a bass player turning cemetery dirt into a dance floor, but funny in the grand old rock-and-roll sense that the concept of memento mori has always looked a little less terrifying once somebody places a wreath of backbeat on the coffin. Made up of Sister Ex alumna Claudia Neuman on bass and vocals, guitarist Anthony Piazza, keyboardist and vocalist Heather Wayward, and drummer Darryl J. Dardenne, the DC/Baltimore group have previously favored the colder end of Gothic psychedelia and glam rock. Graveyard Girl, however, loosens the corset. Funk, garage rock, indie pop and even bossa nova slip into the bloodstream, bringing a loose, easy groove beneath the song’s ’60s pop whimsy while the band keeps one boot planted firmly in post-punk soil. Neuman’s bass is responsible for the initial crime, strutting around with the casual confidence of someone who has found the liquor cabinet during a wake. Wayward’s keyboards add splashes of color around Piazza’s guitar, while Dardenne keeps the song moving with a lightness that gives its cemetery imagery room to grin. The melody has the cheeky charm of a vintage pop single, its tuneful bounce making the invitation to wander among the graves sound suspiciously like a proposition for a Sunday afternoon date. Siouxsie and the Banshees, March Violets, Strange Boutique and more hover somewhere in the family tree, although Winter Sect sound especially amused by the possibilities of their own material here. According to Wayward, that playful turn happened almost accidentally during rehearsal: “The song pretty much started with Claudia grooving out on a bass line,” she says. “It was catchy and I thought let’s do something completely different and not so serious and macabre. First the hook was discovered and we built from there. So with that funk of a groove my mind started walking. Where? Through the graveyard of course. It came together in a cool way and a little twist at the end just makes it fun.” That sense of fun carries into the video, which sends the band wandering through the necropolis in slow motion among candles, veils and fog. Somebody communes with the departed, everybody looks appropriately dressed for the occasion, and the solemn machinery of Gothic imagery gains a sly little wink. You half expect one of the headstones to start keeping time. Watch the video for Graveyard Girl below: Winter Sect began in late 2023 when California native Neuman and Piazza formed the project around feedback-heavy goth, New Wave, industrial and psychedelic influences. Mystic Twin and Haunted House followed in 2024, with Say Goodbye appearing in 2026. Graveyard Girl, taken from the forthcoming EP Offering, suggests Winter Sect have figured out that darkness becomes far more interesting when somebody remembers to leave room for mischief and a tune you can hum on the way home. Listen to Graveyard Girl below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: Winter Sect 由来自 DC/Baltimore 的四位音乐人组成，新单曲 Graveyard Girl 尝试在哥特语境中融入放克、车库摇滚、独立流行甚至巴萨诺瓦的律动元素，将墓地意象与轻松舞动并置。贝斯手 Claudia Neuman 以松弛的律动线条奠定歌曲基调，键盘与吉他在其上点缀色彩，鼓点保持轻盈，使整体呈现出六十年代流行的俏皮质感。歌曲虽然保持后朋克的根基，但在情绪上明显从阴郁转向诙谐，配合慢动作墓地影像，强调暗黑美学中的幽默可能性。这种将哥特传统与多元舞曲节奏融合的写法为乐队带来新的方向，但整体仍属于风格内部的扩展，实验性与突破感有限。

items.body: Town And Towers Records has signed Swiss duo CØLDSTAR, releasing the band’s new single “Last Night On Earth” on 2 October 2026. The track is the Bern-based darkwave, synthpop and coldwave act’s first release on the Danish label. “Last Night On Earth” follows a narrator watching Earth’s final hours from roughly seven hundred miles above the planet, aboard a spacecraft where the oxygen cycles mechanically and the view of the dying world shrinks to a reflection in glass. The lyrics state the moment directly: “The blue marble fades in a rear view of glass / I watch from the silence as centuries pass.” There is no rescue attempt in the story and no final message, only “a velvet curtain, and we’re not coming back.” Dark synth layers, pulsing electronic rhythms and melancholic melodies carry the track’s icy, futuristic atmosphere. Town And Towers names VNV Nation and Black Nail Cabaret as reference points for that sound. Recommend to fans of Solar Fake, Final Selection, Depeche Mode, Covenant and The Soft Moon. CØLDSTAR’s ‘Last Night On Earth’ is the duo’s first release for Town And Towers Records “Last Night On Earth” is out now as a digital single, also streaming via Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, SoundCloud and Tidal. Last Night On Earth by CØLDSTAR Town And Towers Records’ recent roster also includes deZeption, signed in 2024, and Hatif, whose album “Small States” arrived via the label in 2025. About CØLDSTAR Martin Baumann and Michael Freund record as CØLDSTAR from Bern, Switzerland, mixing darkwave, synthpop, coldwave and retro-futurist synth sounds. The duo’s songs use space and science-fiction imagery to address isolation, memory, technology, longing and human existence. CØLDSTAR’s early releases included a 2021 cover of Nine Inch Nails‘ “Hurt.” The band built out its own catalogue with the “Coming Home” EP in 2023, then the debut album “CØSMIC DUST” in 2024 via Swiss Dark Nights, combining atmospheric electronics, synthpop melody and darker post-punk influences. Singles “Time Machine,” “Astronaut’s Lament,” “Last Dance” and “Post-Punk Robot” followed. “Post-Punk Robot” reached number 2 on the Deutsche Alternative Charts in 2026. “Last Night On Earth” is the fifth single CØLDSTAR has issued since “CØSMIC DUST,” and the first through Town And Towers Records.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士双人组CØLDSTAR签约丹麦厂牌Town And Towers Records，发布单曲《Last Night On Earth》。歌曲以七百英里高空的航天器视角旁观地球消亡，歌词描绘蓝色星球在后视镜中褪去、氧气机械循环的末世图景，没有救援也没有遗言，只有天鹅绒帷幕落下。音乐采用暗潮合成器层次、脉冲式电子律动与忧郁旋律，营造冰冷未来感。乐评将其风格参照系锁定在VNV Nation、Black Nail Cabaret，并向Solar Fake、Depeche Mode、Covenant、The Soft Moon等听众推荐。CØLDSTAR此前的作品涵盖2024年专辑《CØSMIC DUST》及多支单曲，主题围绕太空意象、孤独、记忆与人类存在展开，《Last Night On Earth》是该组合第五支单曲，也是厂牌发行的首支作品。整体属于暗潮合成流行的常规制作，主题概念与声响设计具有一定完整性。

items.body: Belgian EBM act Implant releases the EP “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The eight-track release previews the band’s fifteenth studio album, “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” due October 30 on the same label. I’m Only Happy When You Bleed EP by IMPLANT ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ is the second single from ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ The title track is the second song revealed from “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” after lead single “Underneath The Neon Lights.” Built on a 3/4 rhythm, it pairs evolving electronic layers and a shifting pulse with lyrics centered on control, cruelty and forced submission. The EP extends the single into an eight-track release. “Information Systems” opens the record with a long-form soundscape built entirely from spoken samples about the mythology of computing. “The Insider” addresses privileged knowledge and how much of what people take as fact is actually interpretation or assumption. “Pills (in f sharp)” reworks the album track “Pills” into a different key, turning its “I want more pills” refrain into both a chant and a comment on the pursuit of quick fixes. “Underneath The Neon Lights” also appears on the EP. Three remixes of the title track close the release. New York act Crash Course In Science turns the song into a club-oriented dance track. People Theatre take it in a more melodic direction before a detuned lead takes over. Belgian label mate Aiboforcen contributes a version Alfa Matrix describes as distinctly Aiboforcen’s own while staying rooted in Implant’s sound. ‘I’m Only Happy When You Bleed’ EP tracklist “Information Systems” (3:16) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (4:00) “Underneath The Neon Lights” (4:55) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Crash Course In Science remix) (4:39) “Pills (in f sharp)” (4:00) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (People Theatre vein remix) (5:32) “The Insider” (4:33) “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” (Aiboforcen remix) (4:12) The EP is a digital release, available as a download in MP3 and FLAC via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 16-bit/44.1kHz. ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ follows on October 30 Side-Line previously reported on “The Kinematics Of Doubt” in Implant sets 15th album ‘The Kinematics Of Doubt’ for 30 October on Alfa Matrix. The fourteen-track album is issued on CD and digital and includes “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed” alongside “The Observer Effect,” “Underneath The Neon Lights,” “Pills,” “Civilization,” “Sanity,” “Framed,” “Transaction Failure,” “Are You Crying?,” “Talking In Your Sleep,” “Beyond The Code,” “No Apologies Required,” “On TV” and “Wounds.” Implant and Llumen launch their respective albums together on November 20, 2026 at mOtown in Sint-Joost-ten-Node, Belgium. About Implant Implant is the electro-industrial project Len Lemeire started in Belgium in 1996. The debut CD single, “Fun,” credited to Lemeire alongside Geert Machtelinck, was pressed in a numbered edition of 1,000 copies that year. The project’s catalogue spans harsh EBM, industrial dance, electro-pop and dark synth across releases including “Implantology,” “Audio Blender,” “The Productive Citizen” and the EP “Fading Away,” closing most releases with the line “Did you have your Implant today?” Implant released the free download single “The Drive” in December 2023. The twelfth studio album, “The Chaos Machines Part 1 – No More Flies On The Windscreen,” followed in May 2024. Lemeire discussed its modular-synth approach and a duet with Noemi Aurora in Implant interview: ‘Embrace chaos through the machines!’. The trilogy continued with the limited vinyl EP “The Chaos Machines Part 2 – Scratching The Surface” in September 2024 and closed with the album “Judging Sinners – The Chaos Machines Part 3” on February 7, 2025, again featuring Noemi Aurora and covered in Exclusive interview with Implant judging all those sinners. “The Kinematics Of Doubt,” Implant’s fifteenth studio album, follows on October 30, 2026. “I’m Only Happy When You Bleed,” out now as an eight-track EP, is the second single revealed from the record. items._cn_summary: Julia Holter 的新专辑定位为 2024 年《Something In The Room She Moves》的扩展伴侣作品，整体氛围亲密，器乐编排偏向室内乐编制，呈现古典化的织体结构。评论特别指出单曲《Fantasy》带有 Cocteau Twins 式的梦境质感，朦胧绵密的音场处理令人沉醉。作为洛杉矶独立艺术家的作品，她在民谣基底上叠加电子氛围与古典编制的手法具有一定跨界色彩，但评论篇幅较短，仅聚焦于氛围营造与编曲特征，未能深入探讨实验性层面的突破。整体而言，这是一张氛围导向的艺术流行专辑，舒适耐听，但在先锋性与声学探索上略显保守。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There is nothing better than a short, mysterious introduction featuring a siren-like voice to keep the Canterbury spirit alive; that is how "Swedish Love" begins. Much like on Before the Light, the track features sinuous melodies, reminiscent of a roller coaster ride that never stops, even when it momentarily slows down. The English duo consists of Ryan Stevenson, playing piano, synthesizers, Hammond organ, Mellotron, and guitar, and Andrea Moneta on drums and percussion. They are joined by guest flautist Theo Travis (known for his work with Gong and David Sylvian) and Caroline Joy Clarke, who lends her ethereal vocals to the backing harmonies."Eternal Return" showcases National Health's more eccentric compositional side; eschewing classic jazz-rock, it aligns instead with the genre's most esoteric and absurd aspects, both aesthetically and musically. It is also worth highlighting the clever use of contrast between the more energetic, aggressive sections and the more atmospheric ones, such as in "Sanger." "Sellanr�," by contrast, is more minimalist; the piano enters the mix, revealing another facet of the duo that moves beyond mere nostalgia. It is reminiscent of Brian Eno's solo albums from the 1970s.It is on the track "V" that abrasive textures collide with the flute, recalling the alchemy found in the song "Binoculars" from National Health's album Of Queues and Cures. The layering of synthesizers and symphonic arrangements, alongside the Mellotron and a dark-sounding organ, lends the track an orchestral, at times dissonant, sheen, creating one of the album's highlights; comparisons to King Crimson do not seem out of place, either."Being and Time" has a highly dramatic, theatrical atmosphere, driven by the guitar and then a cloud of keyboards that at times reminded me of Present, though without reaching those abyssal extremes. Towards the end, Caroline Joy Clarke's vocals and a Fripp-esque guitar cascade cause that mist to descend to the ground, enveloping everything before the cycle begins anew at "Zero," where a spacey vibe once again takes over the keyboards.In "The Noble Shirker," the bass lines stand out before the guitar enters and the Mellotron joins in, creating a cascading melodic line reminiscent of Mike Oldfield. There is a touch of Eddie Jobson's atmospheric keyboard style, and it is at this point that guest saxophonist Mike Benson joins the mix, adding a new layer of color and warmth. As the sonic haze clears, we witness the transformations at play, a feat of magic and realized esotericism; just as the teapot from the Gong trilogy morphed into a dangerous, lurking scorpion, that saxophone, evoking Mel Collins's work with King Crimson, pushed Zopp's musical intensity to near-maximum velocity.
items._genre: Canterbury Scene / progressive rock / jazz-rock / experimental
items._cn_summary: Zopp是一支英伦二人组合，核心成员为钢琴/键盘手Ryan Stevenson与鼓手Andrea Moneta，辅以长笛（Theo Travis）、女声（Caroline Joy Clarke）及萨克斯（Mike Benson）等客座乐手。专辑延续Canterbury传统，开篇以警笛般的人声制造神秘氛围，后续曲目在钢琴、哈蒙德风琴、Mellotron与合成器之间穿梭，旋律如过山车般起伏。作品在不同曲段间频繁切换质感：既有简洁的极简钢琴段落，也有粗粝质地对撞长笛的段落，结尾以萨克斯铺陈推进，将音乐张力推向高点。整体呈现学院爵士化的前卫摇滚骨架，但在电子实验与暗潮氛围上的拓展有限，更接近对National Health、King Crimson等乐队传统的致敬与重述。
