items.body: La Feria returns to Liverpool this October for its eighth edition, spreading five days of Latin American music, theatre, dance, visual art and food from Hope Street down to Chinatown. The festival was launched in 2018 by Luma Creations, the Liverpool organisation led by Chilean-born songwriter Francisco Carrasco, to put artists from across Latin America and its British diaspora on the city’s stages. This year’s music starts in Chile, with songs built on the Andean rhythms of huayno and tinku and with folk tunes opened up through jazz improvisation. From there it moves to the brass-heavy mambo and salsa dura of a 13-piece Latin big band, to Afro-Colombian gaita flute set over electronic beats and deep bass, and to Brazilian forró and coco rhythms reworked as pop. Around the evening concerts and theatre performances, the week also brings a visual art exhibition, free workshops led by visiting artists, and two free family days to close the festival at the weekend. On Wednesday, Unity Theatre opens the festival with Manuelita, a one-woman show from Popelei in which Tamsin Hurtado Clarke takes on Manuela Sáenz. The Quito-born revolutionary fought through the independence wars at Simón Bolívar’s side, and in 1828 she helped him escape an attempt on his life in Bogotá. Hurtado Clarke tells her story through comedy and physical theatre to music by Colombian guitarist Camilo Menjura. Before the play, 18-year-old Argentine-British musician Eli Rowley plays Argentine and Andean tunes on the ronroco, a big-bodied, low-tuned relative of the charango, taking his cues from Gustavo Santaolalla and Jaime Torres. A short walk from Unity Theatre, the Music Room at Liverpool Philharmonic Hall takes over on Thursday, when Camila y Silvio return after selling out at La Feria in 2022. Camila Soria and Silvio Rozzi met during Chile’s student protests in 2011, and in 2015 they toured Argentina at length, learning the traditional styles of that country and the Andes. Their music moves between huayno, tinku, chacarera and vidala, with two voices over Rozzi’s guitar and charango and the deep thump of Soria’s bombo legüero. Fellow Chileans Peregrinos open the night. Guitarist Raimundo Santander and New York-based drummer Rodrigo Recabarren cut their first record together in Brooklyn in 2013, and they have used Chilean folk material as a starting point for improvisation ever since. By Friday the Music Room’s stage has to make space for thirteen musicians. Orchestra Mambo International came together in 2022 around Leeds salsa DJ Lubi Jovanovic and trombonist Jonny Enright to play the mambo of Tito Puente, Machito and Eddie Palmieri with a full big-band sound. Trumpets, trombone and baritone sax are stacked over piano, bass, vibraphone and a percussion section of bongos, congas and timbales. Since then they have written their own material, from mambos to cha-cha-chás, much of it gathered on their debut album Apúntalo. Up front, Venezuelan singer Carlos Peña, once a featured vocalist in Oscar D’León‘s orchestra, shares the vocals with Cuban singer Claritzel Miyares. It is the band’s first Liverpool show, and Cuban singer-songwriter George Peguero, returning to La Feria, opens the evening. Saturday night belongs to District, the club on Jordan Street in the Baltic Triangle, where Medellín producer Killabeatmaker sets Afro-Colombian and traditional Colombian rhythms over electronic beats and deep bass. His music keeps returning to the wildlife and landscapes of Colombia and the threats they face. On stage he beatboxes, raps and sings over live beats while Guadalupe Giraldo plays percussion and the gaita, the long, breathy duct flute of Colombia’s Caribbean coast. Opening the night, Mari Merenda plays her first ever UK show. The São Paulo singer/songwriter and producer built her name on videos of the asalato, a West African pair of seed-pod shakers knocked together on a cord. Her songs set forró and coco grooves against pop and R&B with electronic touches, most of them from her 2025 EP Reverbero. In Liverpool she switches between piano and asalato, with Guilherme Monteiro on bass, guitar and vocals, before moving on to Brighton and London. Before District opens its doors on Saturday night, World Museum on William Brown Street hands its galleries over to the festival for a free family day of music, dance, storytelling and workshops. The take-over is part of Cuerpos del Tiempo, a project with the museum’s Global Cultures Collections team to reimagine its Americas Gallery. Artists from eleven countries, from Argentina to Venezuela, perform among the displays. At midday Tamachij Chihuatl, a collective of more than 100 Indigenous Nahua women from Hueyapan in Puebla, Mexico, lead a food workshop. For forty years they have kept their village’s textile tradition alive, weaving wool and colouring it with natural dyes, and their name means “handmade”. La Feria’s free finale takes over The Black-E, the community arts centre on Great George Street, on Sunday. There, Orkney fiddler Catriona Price plays with El Guapo, a Buenos Aires duo on guitar, drums, percussion and vocals who mix Latin American roots with rock and funk. Together they run Routes to Roots, a project that brings musicians from different cultures together to write new music and rework traditional tunes, and which took them to the Edinburgh International Festival in August. Three dance companies share the day. London’s ArtPer UK bring Peruvian folk dances from the coast, the Andes and the Amazon, including the marinera norteña, a courtship dance in which couples circle each other waving handkerchiefs. Colibrí, a Manchester troupe of Mexican dancers led by Guerrero-born choreographer Magaly Flores, perform regional dances in traditional costume, from Veracruz and the Huasteca down to Oaxaca and Chiapas. Inti Tusuy, whose name is Quechua for “sun dance”, bring together dancers with roots in Bolivia, Mexico, Peru and the UK. Latin American food, DJs and dance workshops fill out the afternoon. Once the music stops at The Black-E on Sunday afternoon, the festival’s 2026 theme stays on the walls at Unity Theatre. Belonging, an exhibition by UK-based artists of Latin American heritage, runs there until 6th November, with work drawn from diaspora, ancestry and the places its makers call home.   Full programme and tickets are on the La Feria website The post Event Preview: La Feria 2026 (Liverpool; Wednesday 7th to Sunday 11th October 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Two newly reissued albums showcase the seismic psychedelia of George Clinton’s Funkadelic at its rawest and most disruptive, writes John Morrison in The Wire 512 Funkadelic Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Maggot Brain Westbound/Org CD/DL/LP/2xLP/MC Released the summer before Jimi Hendrix tragically passed away in 1970, Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow was not only the follow-up to Funkadelic’s promising self-titled debut of the same year; it signalled the arrival of George Clinton’s ensemble as the next great voice in Black rock and psychedelia. In his 2014 memoir Brothas Be, Yo Like George, Ain’t That Funkin’ Kinda Hard On You?, Clinton acknowledges this by contrasting the album’s release with Hendrix’s death, an event that he notes as “the end of an era”. During his brief but electrifying career, Hendrix moulded multiple aspects of the Black musical tradition – blues, rock, funk, R&B, jazz – into an electrifying corpus that opened up a new world of possibilities. With Hendrix dead and the psychedelic road map that he laid out for any adventurous soul to follow, Funkadelic went on to emerge as his mightiest descendents. While Funkadelic were recording Free Your Mind Clinton absorbed and pulled inspiration from underground comics, Black power/radical leftist theory and Erich von Däniken’s work theorising that aliens had made contact with and shaped the development of ancient human civilisations. Clinton took all the disparate cultural, historical, political and extraterrestrial influences swirling around in his head and drenched them in acid. The famously LSD soaked sessions produced an album that distilled the political, cultural and philosophical DNA of the 1960s into a new musical vision for the 70s. Built around Eddie Hazel’s gnarly blues and wah-wah drenched guitar, “Funky Dollar Bill” highlights the flipside of the concept of money as freedom explored on “Friday Night, August 14th”. With lyrics like "The pusher push, the fixer fix, the judge acquits, the junkie leads his life, for the dollar bill”, it's clear that here, money is less a vehicle for freedom than a tool for control. “Eulogy And Light” serves as the perfect album closer, with Clinton praying for strength in the face of temptation and moral degradation. In an innovative display of the band's willingness to experiment with sound and concepts, the music for “Eulogy And Light” is an earlier Funkadelic track called “Open Your Eyes” spun backwards. In doing this, Clinton and crew extract the source song's optimistic heart and repurpose its gospel-inspired tune into something stranger, more twisted. Free Your Mind opens with the epic ten minute title track. Amid a ghostly mass of distorted guitar, feedback and cosmic synthesizer bleeps, Clinton screams “Free your mind and your ass will follow/The kingdom of heaven is within!”. These simple yet spine-tingling chants formed something close to a succinct mission statement. More than just slogans, Clinton was directly addressing the intellectual, physical and spiritual demands of a new musical and ideological path. He has described “Friday Night, August 14th” as a “paycheck and party song” about how a little bit of money can buy a moment of joy and freedom. In that sense, the song feels like the spiritual heir to Louis Jordan's 1949 proto-rock ’n’ roll smash “Saturday Night Fish Fry”. By the time Funkadelic entered the United Sound Systems studio in Detroit to record the follow-up to Free Your Mind, the band were at once a formidable live unit and boundless experimenters in the studio. The result of those USS sessions was 1971’s Maggot Brain, one of the greatest psychedelic rock albums ever made and the crown jewel of Clinton’s extensive body of work. The album opens with a simple and ominous message that is both a continuation of the core theme examined throughout Free Your Mind and a harbinger of the band’s future: “I have tasted the maggots in the mind of the universe/I was not offended/For I knew I had to rise above it all/Or drown in my own shit”. Here the “maggots” are the corrosive forces of ignorance, self-doubt and control that infested Free Your Mind. To all intents and purposes, Maggot Brain is a trip through the other side of enlightenment, witnessed through the prism of life, death and the liberatory potential of madness. Famously, Clinton prompted guitarist Eddie Hazel to imagine that his mother had died before recording Maggot Brain’s almost ten minute long title track. Hazel transforms his guitar into a wailing and mourning instrument of grief. Beneath his solo, a dreamy, six note arpeggio acts as the bedrock to one of the greatest guitar performances ever captured on tape. “Can You Get To That” flips the energy from dark to light with its slick groove and doo-wop harmonies. A bright and joyous song at face value, the lyrics warn that even in death, no one escapes karma. “Hit It And Quit It” is a flamboyant acid rock tune with an odd metre that betrays Funkadelic's debt to both the church and the temple of Jimi Hendrix. For an outfit that proved so adept at conjuring colourful, funky images of utopia, it's curious that they chose to close out their greatest album with “Wars Of Armageddon”. Clocking in at over nine minutes long, the song is a minefield of explosions, screams and fuzzed-out guitars. The chants of “More power to the people/More pussy to the power” offer a reminder that Funkadelic’s psychedelic ideals and ambitions never strayed too far from the funky, carnal physicality of life on Earth. This review appears in The Wire 512 along with many other reviews of new and recent records, books, films, festivals and more. To read them all, pick up a copy of the magazine in our online shop. Wire subscribers can also read the issue in our online magazine library.
items._cn_summary: 这张1970年发行的专辑是George Clinton率领的Funkadelic第二张录音室作品，承接首作同名专辑的势头，确立了乐队作为黑人摇滚与迷幻音乐领域重要声音的地位。录制过程深受LSD影响，George Clinton将地下漫画、黑人权力运动、激进左翼理论以及关于外星文明的假说等多元文化养分灌注其中。吉他手Eddie Hazel以粗粝的蓝调音色与wah-wah效果器堆叠出迷幻音墙，合成器与失真反馈交织成宇宙感的声场。专辑以同名十分钟史诗开篇，歌曲中将一首早期作品倒放处理，提取其原本乐观的福音旋律内核，将其扭曲为更加怪异的形态，体现出乐队对声音实验与概念创新的执着。歌词层面尖锐批判金钱作为控制工具的本质，并以祈祷式的尾声收束全作，将六十年代的政治、文化与哲学基因蒸馏为面向七十年代的新音乐愿景。

items.body: Label: Endectomorph Records, 2026 Personnel - Kenny Warren: trumpet; Adam Schneit: alto saxophone, clarinet; JP Schlegelmilch: organ; Andrew Dow: electric bass; Nathan Ellman-Bell: drums. Slow Tiger—the jazz quintet of trumpeter Kenny Warren, saxophonist and clarinetist Adam Schneit, organist JP Schlegelmilch, electric bassist Andrew Dow, and drummer Nathan Ellman-Bell—releases its debut album, pointing in many directions with an impeccable flow and assured tones. All its members, with the exception of Ellman-Bell, contribute compositions, filtering influences through the lens of this cohesive collective ensemble. Melodies stick on the ear as the band, whose prior successful collaborations led to the album, leans toward a pop/rock style that easily accommodates jazz-leaning improvisation. Warren's " Powerpuff Backpack " is a tribute to late trumpeter Ron Miles, revealing traces of folk and funk woven into the framework of pop and psychedelic rock infusions. Occasionally, bands like Inspiral Carpets and Jethro Tull come to mind, and Schneit's clarinet explores with effortless inside/outside agility, followed by Warren, who also brings in " Eleven Six ”. Its title comes from the fact that Ellman-Bell plays a cymbal pulsation in eleven while Dow shapes an upbeat six-beat bass figure that provides solid ground for the horn players to interact. They exchange ideas with grip and avant-garde stance, while Schlegelmilch makes the piece soar via hypnotic organ waves and ostinato-leaning textures that add dimension to the music. Schneit, who was born in Portland, Maine, named " Wharf Street " after the street where he grew up. This is a pop tune permeated with a strong 60's vibe, with the composer and Warren intersecting phrases with insouciant power, precision, but also freedom. They also bring this strategy to Schlegelmilch's time-shifting " Maritime Studies ”, which is buttressed by a sluggish beat and cautiously measured unisons. The organist's response to the pandemic's forced pause comes with " Mending the Nets ”, a gentle waltzing ballad moved by sizzling brushes, melancholic melody, and church-like organ sustains. The quintet aligns in relaxed sounds on the title track, " Slow Tiger ", a soulful, melodically seductive piece romanticized by warm R&B colors. It contrasts with Dow's " Funhouse ", whose groove in nine defines the tempo. With the organ illuminating the scenario with crested ripples of sound, the piece morphs into openly avant-garde territory as the horns criss-cross atop the rhythmic net laced by bass and drums. Slow Tiger shows potential, and its debut is a tantalizing promise of more albums to come. Favorite Tracks: 02 - Maritime Studies ► 05 - Eleven in Six ► 07 - Funhouse ► 09 - Slow Tiger
items._cn_summary: Slow Tiger的首张同名专辑由五位爵士乐手组成，涵盖小号、萨克斯、单簧管、风琴、电贝斯与鼓的编制。乐队以流行摇滚框架为基底，融入自由即兴、前卫爵士与迷幻摇滚元素，在结构与即兴之间寻求平衡。多首曲目探索不对称节拍与复节奏组合，如十一拍对六拍的对话，以及九拍的复合律动。风琴作为和声与色彩核心，提供持续的催眠质感与教堂般的延音层次。作品涵盖向已故小号手Ron Miles致敬的放克民谣融合曲、六十年代怀旧流行调、以及在深渊稳健前行前即兴场域中自由穿梭的开放段落。整体展现乐队的合奏默契与即兴张力，是一张兼具旋律可听性与实验野心的首作。

Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑围绕俄罗斯强行带走约两万乌克兰儿童的战争罪行展开，Marichka与加拿大全女性团体Daughters of Donbas联合乌克兰和加拿大两组乐手共同录制。音乐以传统弦乐、班杜拉琴、钢琴为主，混声合唱与对位编排贯穿全作，既有改编自乌克兰传统民歌的曲目，也有原创作品。歌词多取自传统仪式歌曲与历史民谣，将当代议题嵌入古老的叙事框架。整张专辑在音乐性与人文关怀之间寻求平衡，文本与旋律的结合构成专辑的核心张力。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._genre: Benin funk / Afro-Cuban / vodun rhythm / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌继此前三张Poly-Rythmo合辑后，首次将视角聚焦于贝宁歌手兼作曲家Antoine Dougbè的个人作品。Dougbè以双手拍腿的Cavacha节奏闻名，这一节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节拍中提炼，后蔓延至1970年代中期的刚果流行乐坛。Dougbè本人是伏都教信仰者，自称"魔鬼首相"，专挑Poly-Rythmo合作，认为只有他们能精准实现其构想。本合辑收录其短暂生涯的三张专辑及若干单曲，跨越1977至1982年。编曲上融合古巴颂、刚果伦巴与西非伏都律动，合成器与塑料质感的吉他音色交织，呈现八十年代特有的干燥声景。从世界音乐角度出发，这张专辑展现了非洲本土节奏体系与拉丁美洲、加勒比元素的深层对话。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组 GuldGanger 的首张数字 EP，由北欧民谣圈经验丰富的歌手 Mia Guldhammer 领衔，收录五首曲目。乐评描述整张作品弥漫着古老、粗糙的氛围，开场曲以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；口簧与风笛为唯一的原创曲带来强劲推进力；扬琴为传统曲目营造精致背景；终曲则以口簧、长笛与弦乐的交织形成离奇而动人的器乐表达。乐评认为乐队虽刚出道却显得成熟老练，对完整专辑充满期待。整体偏向北欧传统民谣，带有实验性的器乐编排与非常规乐器组合，属于世界音乐范畴内较有特色的跨界尝试。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / soundscape
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统音乐作品，而是由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述记录。录制地点是一位94岁祖母家门前的前廊，正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队当天。参与者从17岁到67岁不等，共25人讲述亲身经历，包括一位失去两个儿子的老人反复道歉的画面。专辑不加任何音乐伴奏，保留环境声如蚊虫和飞机降落声。其艺术价值在于用声音原貌呈现被遗忘社区的真实生活，与世界音乐、田野录音、现场记录的实验传统有交集。收益捐赠给以公共卫生方法遏制暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。

items.body: Review by Warthur — This is Jack Bruce's firet solo album, at least in terms of release date - the Things We Like jamsession was recorded prior to this and released as a follow-up. I've never fully gotten onboard withCream, and maybe it's Eric Clapton that's the component that doesn't quite land for me, becausebetween Ginger Baker's work elsewhere and now this I can say I'm more impressed with the other Creammembers' solo fare than Clapton's.What you get here is bluesy art rock with brilliant bass lines and poetic lyrics by Pete Brown. Somesongs on here ended up travelling widely, with Mountain, Colosseum, and Greenslade covering farelike Theme From An Imaginary Western or Rope Ladder To the Moon; others definitely qualify as deepcuts. Either way, well worth exploring.
items._genre: blues rock / art rock / jazz rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Jack Bruce的首张正式个人专辑，由Cream乐队的贝斯手独立完成。整体定位为带有爵士色彩的蓝调艺术摇滚，以出色的贝斯演奏和Pete Brown充满诗意的歌词为核心特色。专辑中部分曲目后来被Mountain、Colosseum和Greenslade等乐队翻唱传播，如《Theme From An Imaginary Western》和《Rope Ladder To the Moon》，其余则是较为冷门的深度曲目。编曲上融合了布鲁斯摇滚的即兴段落与艺术摇滚的结构感，贝斯线条贯穿始终成为主导乐器。从用户口味来看，这张专辑虽然带有一定的爵士融合色彩和艺术摇滚气质，但缺乏明显的实验性、前卫性或电子元素，更偏向传统摇滚框架内的即兴演奏，与用户偏爱的实验前卫、学院派爵士、电子音乐等方向存在一定距离。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统乐评，而是《The Wire》杂志旗下电台节目的单曲列表与播放清单，涵盖Don Cherry、Glass Triangle、Agnes Haus、Ziûr等十余组艺人的作品。这些曲目横跨自由即兴、实验电子、噪音与当代作曲等多个领域，涉及的厂牌包括Relative Pitch、LINE、Pressure、Constellation Tatsu等独立小众发行。选曲体现策展人James Gormley对前卫声音的广泛涉猎——从Don Cherry 1977年现场录音中融合世界音乐元素的自由爵士，到Hellhound等地下金属乐队的极端声响，再到Ziûr为舞蹈表演创作的原声带。整份清单作为广播节目的推介，展示了一档专注于实验音乐生态的周播节目的内容广度与选曲取向。

items.body: Pygmy Children reissue their 1994 debut album “Malignant” as “Malignant: Redux” via Re:Mission Entertainment. The label describes the release as electro-industrial and EBM, with a release date of October 2, 2026. The original “Malignant” was recorded by Brian Roper and Pete Roper at Hit And Run Studios in Rockville, Maryland, between September and December 1993, and released on CD via Noname/Noslogan Productions in 1994 with an 11-track listing running from “Shock V3.1” through “File Regarding…”. “Malignant: Redux” adds five further tracks to that original running order. Re:Mission Entertainment has not published a description of what the “Redux” edition changes beyond its expanded tracklist; that detail is not yet confirmed. Malignant : Redux by Pygmy Children About Pygmy Children Pygmy Children is a US electro-industrial project built around Brian Roper and Pete Roper, active since the early 1990s. The duo released their debut album “Malignant” in 1994, followed by “Low Life Dream” in 1998. After a long gap, Pygmy Children returned through Re:Mission Entertainment with the EP “I Have No Name”, the single “Proof in Lies”, the “Signal Unknown” EP and the album “Coincidental Strategies”. “Malignant: Redux”, out October 2, 2026, revisits the project’s debut album more than three decades after its original release.
items._cn_summary: Pygmy Children 是来自美国的双人电子工业项目，由Brian Roper 和 Pete Roper 组成，自九十年代初活跃至今。其1994年首张专辑《Malignant》由马里兰州Hit And Run Studios录制，曲目从"Shock V3.1"延伸至"File Regarding…"，共十一首，展现了早期EBM与工业电子的典型形态。2026年通过Re:Mission Entertainment再版的《Malignant: Redux》在保留原始曲目顺序基础上新增五首作品，构成扩展版发行。作为对三十余年前首作的重访，这张再版为老听众提供了补充素材，也是了解九十年代美式工业场景的入口之一。原版与再版之间细节差异尚未由厂牌公布，因此新版在混音、制作层面的具体改动仍不明确。整体而言，这是一次面向小众受众的档案性发行，适合对早期电子工业场景感兴趣、尤其是赵美式回归厂牌Re:Mission Entertainment厂牌后续作品的听众。

items.body: Tangent Strategy announces “Tristesse”, the project’s first new full-length album in five years. The album is inspired by the music of John Foxx and Die Form. “Tristesse” explores the fragile human psyche, where anger and melancholy sit next to each other. It looks at the defiance inside relationships, healthy and unhealthy alike, and the marks they leave on the people in them. Production-wise, the album takes a simpler approach than before, keeping the songs raw with deep bass, stark arrangements and noise running through the mix. “In an age of detachment, Tristesse is a reminder that attachment is no certain comfort either,” the project states. Tristesse by Tangent Strategy About Tangent Strategy Tangent Strategy was formed in 1996 by chd.y as an outlet for a musical outlook that grew more and more drawn to industrial music over the years. The project’s first full-length, “Revenant”, came out in November 2021 via EK Product. Since then, chd.y has released several EPs under the name and performed live in Tokyo. “Tristesse”, announced in 2026, is Tangent Strategy’s second full-length album.
items._cn_summary: Tangent Strategy时隔五年推出第二张全长唱片《Tristesse》，灵感来自John Foxx与Die Form的音乐传统。项目自1996年由chd.y创立，长期致力于工业音乐方向，首张全长《Revenant》于2021年通过EK Product发行。新作在制作上转向更为简洁的路径，保留深沉的贝斯线条、克制的编曲结构以及贯穿混音的粗砺声响。专辑主题围绕人类心理的脆弱层面展开，探讨愤怒与忧郁的共存、关系中的叛逆与伤痕。整体呈现出一种内省式的工业暗潮美学，强调情感依附与疏离之间的张力，与创作者此前作品相比更为原始和直接。

The nine-track record sat unfinished for years, surfacing only after a self-titled Sevit album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” runs nine tracks: Ode To A Requiem Beyond My Control Escape Dreamland In So Many Words It Must Be Berlin Until Sundown The Happy Crowd The Walls Are Closing In (Original Version) Re
items.body: Sevit released “Requiem”, a darkwave album the Dallas-area duo wrote as the follow-up to 2021’s “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” on 1 October 2026. The nine-track record sat unfinished for years, surfacing only after a self-titled Sevit album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” runs nine tracks: Ode To A Requiem Beyond My Control Escape Dreamland In So Many Words It Must Be Berlin Until Sundown The Happy Crowd The Walls Are Closing In (Original Version) Requiem Requiem by Sevit Sevit have not detailed why the record was set aside, but the band summed up the gap in one line: “Maybe some records simply have to wait until the people who created them finally catch up with them.” Sevit’s ‘Requiem’ follows ‘On The Edge Of A Darker Place’ “Requiem” is out now on Bandcamp as a digital release. About Sevit Jackie Legos (vocals, guitar) and Cam B. (synths, programming) write and record Sevit from the Dallas, Texas area, where the duo formed in 2020 after both had played in earlier North Texas bands, including At Night and Pleasure Crisis. They issued the “A Darker Place” EP that same year and signed to Peru’s InClub Records that October. Sevit’s debut album, “On The Edge Of A Darker Place,” arrived in September 2021: thirteen tracks that draw on The Cure, Joy Division, Bauhaus and Siouxsie & The Banshees, played live by a five-piece band built around the Legos and Cam B. core. Jackie Legos has described the band’s lyrics as rooted in “poetry, and things that might have directly and indirectly crossed my path in life.” The duo wrote “Requiem” as that album’s direct sequel, then set it aside. A self-titled album filled the gap in 2024. “Requiem” finally surfaces, closing a chapter the band had otherwise left open.
items._cn_summary: Sevit 是来自美国得克萨斯州达拉斯地区的二人组合，由 Jackie Legos 担任人声与吉他，Cam B. 负责合成器与编程。《Requiem》原本计划作为 2021 年首张专辑《On The Edge Of A Darker Place》的直接续作而创作，却因故搁置数年，期间由 2024 年的同名专辑填补空白，直到 2026 年 10 月才以数字形式在 Bandcamp 发行。专辑共九首曲目，风格延续乐队对 The Cure、Joy Division、Bauhaus 与 Siouxsie & The Banshees 等后朋克与暗潮经典的汲取，人声与合成器构成作品的主体框架。乐队成员将歌词视为个人生活经验与诗意的交汇。整张专辑更接近对传统暗潮语汇的延续，而非对类型边界的拓展。

The track pushes vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler’s electronic side further forward, bringing futurepop and synthwave into the project’s established synthpop sound, with Siegler citing VNV Nation and Chvrches among t
items.body: The Pixel Rain released “Glitching Sky” on October 2, 2026, the fourth and final advance single from the Southeast London act’s debut album, “A Sense of Danger,” due October 29 on Bandcamp, Spotify and other digital platforms. The track pushes vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler’s electronic side further forward, bringing futurepop and synthwave into the project’s established synthpop sound, with Siegler citing VNV Nation and Chvrches among the single’s reference points. At the center of the song is a character retreating from an unfulfilling reality into a virtual world where he can construct a more powerful version of himself. Siegler extends the idea beyond any specific technology or platform to a broader comment on how people seek distraction from anxiety, disappointment and everyday life. Siegler describes the retreat as carrying both sadness and absurdity: “The idea came from thinking about someone whose real life isn’t giving them very much, so they retreat into a virtual world where they can be whoever they want to be. There’s something quite sad about that, but also something a little ridiculous, so I wanted the story to have both sides to it. “I deliberately left the virtual world undefined because I think that kind of escape can take a lot of different forms. I’m certainly not outside of it myself. We all have things we disappear into when reality gets uncomfortable. “The music is quite fast and energetic, but the song itself takes its time building. That seemed to fit the idea: you don’t necessarily notice yourself getting drawn further and further into these little distractions until they’ve started taking up much more of your life than you intended.” The single arrives with a visualizer by Sophie Maria Vickers, built around the song’s virtual setting and digital imagery. Glitching Sky by The Pixel Rain On Bandcamp, “Glitching Sky” is bundled together with The Pixel Rain’s three earlier advance singles, “Last,” “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice.” The single is also on Spotify and other major platforms. About The Pixel Rain The Pixel Rain is the solo project of vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler, originally from Hungary and now based in Southeast London. The project emerged from London’s underground scene with a self-titled debut EP in 2023, and mixes dark electronic and post-punk elements with guitar, electronics and industrial textures. The Pixel Rain released the first single from its forthcoming debut album, “Last,” on June 19, 2026, with a video shot in Hungary in which Siegler was joined on screen by Balázs Fűr, András Melles, Máté Breier and Máté Király-Gyeőry. The singles “A Sense of Danger” and “Sacrifice” followed over the summer, each previewing the album further. “Glitching Sky,” released October 2, 2026, is the fourth and final advance single before the debut album “A Sense of Danger” arrives on October 29, 2026. The album explores power, authority, consumerism and social unease through recurring post-apocalyptic and technological imagery.
items._cn_summary: The Pixel Rain 是由来自匈牙利、定居伦敦东南部的歌手兼多乐器演奏者 Áron Siegler 主持的个人计划，作品融合暗潮电子与后朋克元素，辅以吉他、工业质感纹理。这首"Glitching Sky"是其首张专辑《A Sense of Danger》发行前的第四支也是最后一支先行单曲，风格在既定合成器流行基础上向未来流行与合成器波方向推进，参考对象包括 VNV Nation 和 Chvrches。歌曲围绕一个角色从失意的现实退入虚拟世界、重塑更强自我的叙事展开，刻意不限定虚拟世界的具体形态，将其泛化为现代人逃避焦虑与日常挫败感的普遍行为。创作者将这种逃避描述为兼具悲伤与荒诞的双重质感，音乐节奏明快紧凑，但歌曲结构层层递进，模拟不知不觉沉溺于分心的过程。视觉部分由 Sophie Maria Vickers 担纲，围绕虚拟设定与数字意象构建。整体属于独立场景中的电子流行创作，主题触及数字时代逃避主义，有一定思考深度，但音乐本身的实验性与声音设计突破有限。

items.album: My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult’s ‘The Reincarnation of Luna’ turns 25 on 2 October
items.excerpt: Chicago industrial dance band My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult released “The Reincarnation of Luna” on 2 October 2001 through SleazeBox Records, the band’s own label, distributed by Invisible Records. The album turns 25 this year. My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult recorded and mixed the album at Starlust Studios in Los Angeles, with Buzz McCoy producing. Groovie Mann and Buzz McCoy wrote all twelve tracks, performed with the Bomb Gang Girlz, and Chris Greene handled mastering.
items.body: Chicago industrial dance band My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult released “The Reincarnation of Luna” on 2 October 2001 through SleazeBox Records, the band’s own label, distributed by Invisible Records. The album turns 25 this year. My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult recorded and mixed the album at Starlust Studios in Los Angeles, with Buzz McCoy producing. Groovie Mann and Buzz McCoy wrote all twelve tracks, performed with the Bomb Gang Girlz, and Chris Greene handled mastering. The tracklist runs: “Radio Silicon” “The Untouchable Class” “Hour of Zero” “The Kult Konnection” “Girl Without a Planet” “Temptation Serenade” “Bettie” “Flesh Playhouse” “Heelz Afire” “Jungle of Love” “Asylum Disciple” “Theme De Luna” “The Reincarnation of Luna” was My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult’s first release on their own SleazeBox Records imprint, following “A Crime for All Seasons” (1997) on Red Ant Records. The band released a companion remix set, “Golden Pillz: The Luna Remixes,” and a live album, “Elektrik Inferno,” in the same period. In 2007, the band re-recorded and remixed the album for Rykodisc under the title “The Resurrection of Luna,” adding “Ocean of Hate,” “Hallowed Be My Name” and a remix of “Temptation Serenade.” The original 2001 version remains available through the band’s own site. About My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult, often shortened to Thrill Kill Kult or TKK, formed in Chicago in 1987. Groovie Mann (born Frankie Nardiello) and Buzz McCoy (born Marston Daley) met that year while touring with Ministry and began recording music for an unfinished art film of the same name. Wax Trax! Records released the completed songs as a three-track EP, and when it sold well, the full-length “I See Good Spirits and I See Bad Spirits” followed in 1988. “Confessions of a Knife…” (1990) became one of Wax Trax!’s best-selling releases, and “Sexplosion!” (1991) pushed the band toward a more psychedelic house and disco sound while drawing attention from Interscope Records, which signed the band and released the alternative-radio single “Sex on Wheelz.” “13 Above the Night” (1993) and “Hit & Run Holiday” (1995) followed on Interscope before the band parted ways with the label in 1996. “A Crime for All Seasons” (1997) came out on Red Ant Records, and “The Reincarnation of Luna” (2001) marked the start of the band’s own SleazeBox Records imprint, distributed by Invisible Records. Rykodisc later became the band’s home, reissuing its back catalog alongside the rarities set “Dirty Little Secrets,” the mash-up album “Diamonds & Daggerz” (2004) and the long-shelved “Gay, Black and Married” (2005). SleazeBox partnered with Italy’s Rustblade label in 2009, issuing “Blood + Dope + Sin + Gold” (2008), “Death Threat” (2009) and “Sinister Whisperz” (2011), and Side-Line covered the band’s 2020 “Sinister Whisperz” retrospective installment, “The Rykodisc Years.” Buzz McCoy has also remixed tracks for KMFDM, Pigface and other acts, and recorded as Excessive Force with KMFDM’s Sascha Konietzko. The band has contributed songs to film soundtracks including “Cool World” (1992), “The Crow” (1994), in which members also appeared performing in a nightclub scene, “The Flintstones” (1994), “Showgirls” (1995) and “Baseketball” (1998). My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult toured the US in spring 2026 with support from Heavy Halo, as Side-Line reported at the time, continuing to perform a catalog that this October marks the 25th anniversary of “The Reincarnation of Luna.”
items._cn_summary: 本文为Side-Line杂志发布的纪念性新闻稿，介绍芝加哥工业舞曲乐队My Life with the Thrill Kill Kult 2001年专辑《The Reincarnation of Luna》发行25周年。文章详细列出了专辑的录制信息、厂牌背景、完整曲目列表以及乐队的历史沿革，从Wax Trax!时代到Interscope签约时期，再到自创厂牌SleazeBox Records的历程。专辑融合了工业舞曲与迷幻浩室元素，由Groovie Mann与Buzz McCoy创作完成，还包括一张配套混音作品《Golden Pillz》以及现场专辑《Elektrik Inferno》。2007年乐队对全作进行了重新录制并追加三首曲目。整体而言，该作品属于暗潮与工业舞曲领域较为典型的类型制作，文章以信息梳理为主，并未涉及深入的音乐分析或美学评价。

items.body: Belgian electronic artist Franky Deblomme releases a new EP as Cubic, “Elements,” on October 2, 2026 via Alfa Matrix. The five-track digital release moves the project’s minimal electro sound into more dynamic techno territory. Elements EP by CUBIC ‘Elements’ draws on 80s electro, 90s techno and dub techno “Elements” draws on 1980s electro, 1990s techno in the style of R&S Records, and acid and dub techno, the reference points that have run through Cubic’s sound over the years, with Alfa Matrix noting a nod toward contemporary acts such as Bicep and Modeselektor. Opening track “Future Past” and the two versions of “BangBang,” a Detroit edit and a Chicago edit, push the EP toward a more dancefloor-oriented, energetic direction. “A Fish” and “Chord Memory” keep the minimal sequences, vintage electronics and repeating patterns that recur through Cubic’s releases. ‘Elements’ EP tracklist “Future Past” (4:31) “BangBang” (Detroit edit) (4:26) “A Fish” (4:35) “Chord Memory” (4:55) “BangBang” (Chicago edit) (4:10) The EP is a digital release, available as a download via the Alfa Matrix Bandcamp page, with streaming included, at up to 24-bit/44.1kHz. About Cubic Cubic is the electronic project of Belgian artist Franky Deblomme, also known for his earlier work as 808 Dot Pop. Deblomme signed Cubic to Alfa Matrix and released the project’s label debut EP, “Alphabet Hymn,” on March 9, 2021. The five-track EP combined vintage Dusseldorf synth influences, Berlin techno, 1990s Manchester rave and EBM, built entirely on hardware synthesizers and effects at Deblomme’s Bong 13 studio, and included a remix by label mates 808 Dot Pop. Later that month, Cubic reworked an earlier 808 Dot Pop album into “The Cubic Temperature,” released March 26, 2021 with an exclusive Bandcamp megamix bonus track. Cubic’s debut album, “The Cubic Alphabet,” arrived on June 18, 2021. The project continued with the EP “Phonic Lessons Part 3” on December 7, 2021, then the singles “Exit – Frankfurt” on April 7, 2022 and the four-track “Exit – Ghent” on June 29, 2022, each tied to a specific city’s electronic scene. The EPs “c64” (September 18, 2023) and “c128” (December 6, 2023), both referencing Commodore home computers, preceded the album “Back To Basic,” released on Alfa Matrix on June 4, 2024 with a Kraftwerk-indebted sound made using the first Belgian-made drum computer (Modor DR2) and synthesizer (Modor NF1). Cubic released the vinyl EP “EFM01 (Black)” in an ultra-limited run in June 2025, then the digital EP “EFM02” in October 2025 and the rework album “Back To 808” in December 2025. The twin EPs “CB-708” and “CB-128,” revisiting “Back To 808,” came out in February 2026. “Elements,” out October 2, 2026, is Cubic’s newest EP on Alfa Matrix. items._cn_summary: 比利时电子艺术家Franky Deblomme以Cubic名义在Alfa Matrix厂牌发行五曲EP《Elements》，延续其minimal electro路线并向更具动感的techno方向拓展。作品融合80年代electro、90年代techno、R&S厂牌风格、acid与dub techno元素，参考Bicep和Modeselektor等当代艺人。开篇曲《Future Past》与《BangBang》的Detroit及Chicago两个版本呈现舞曲化、能量化的走向，而《A Fish》与《Chord Memory》保留了贯穿Cubic作品的极简序列、复古电子音色与重复pattern结构。全作在比利时音乐人Bong 13工作室以硬件合成器与效果器制作完成，涵盖五首时长约四分钟上下的曲目，以24-bit数字格式发行。该EP延续了艺术家自首张EP《Alphabet Hymn》以来的城市主题（法兰克福、根特）与硬件复古路线，是其在minimal electro与techno交界地带的一次平衡探索。

items.body: What’s old is always new again. We got a full-blown nü metal revival on our hands, noise rock is arguably as popular as it’s ever been, and Myspace-era metalcore is getting about as many new releases from bands with members who were born around the same time the legends were laying the foundation. I was also recently reminded that fucking Greta Van Fleet exists for some godforsaken reason. For some other reason, I feel like we’ve just kinda skipped over a lot of good stuff. Where’s the grunge revival? Where’s the college-rock revival? Where’s the early post-punk revival? Where’s all the shit that sounds like it was made by people who hadn’t yet figured out what genre they were supposed to be in? Why does everyone nowadays sound so ready to be categorized?Well, Whippets make a case to step into these shoes, sounding something like Unwound by way of Dinosaur Jr. and Jay Reatard, or like Fugazi covering Dismemberment Plan and Siouxsie and the Banshees at the same time. They convey this volatile energy with writhing guitar leads that are often as eerie as they are anthemic, and tuneful bass in a rhythm section that paves the way for both their most unruly and airy moments. Much like their 2024 self-titled release, Whippets again flex their knack for melodies that get their hooks in your eardrums like velcro. No Skulls is every bit as fearless and without boundaries, gaining traction across a multitude of late 80s and early 90s soundscapes, regularly finding familiar touchpoints with the intuition to pull the rug at just the right time, or mix ‘n’ match influences in a way that’s as much “Aha!” as it is “What the fuck?” It’s like post-punk found the perfectly imperfect dancing partner in shoegaze, distraught while still finding an endearing footing, abrasive, oddly charming, and eyebrow-raising all at once.The video for album opener “These Woods” taps into a similar throwback, like it could’ve been dug out of a shoebox full of forgotten tapes and old zines. With a hazy camcorder look, sunbleached and spliced together with live footage, BMXers, scrapbook imagery, and other ’90s feels, it has the scrappy and surreal feel of something you might’ve stumbled across on MTV’s 120 Minutes at 1 a.m. It’s an appropriate visual companion, familiar enough to trigger a deeply buried memory, but weird enough to feel like you’ve never quite seen it before—and maybe even inspire a bad haircut.Check it out: No Skulls drops today, October 2, on wax and digital via No Coast Records.
items._genre: post-punk / noise rock / shoegaze / indie rock
items._cn_summary: Whippets首张专辑《No Skulls》融合了后朋克、噪音摇滚与瞪鞋元素，吉他音色在粗粝与梦幻间切换，贝斯线条推动节奏起伏，整体介于八十年代末至九十年代初的另类摇滚美学之间。乐评指出乐队不拘泥于单一类型标签，将Unwound、Dinosaur Jr.、Fugazi等乐队的影响解构重组，在熟悉的旋律结构上不断制造出人意料的转折。专辑主打单曲《These Woods》的MV采用九十年代录像带质感，混杂BMX车手、剪贴簿素材，营造出深夜MTV《120 Minutes》节目的怀旧氛围。这张专辑在复古情绪与粗糙质地之间寻找平衡，编曲上展现了一定的拼贴意识，但对追求前沿实验声响的听众而言，其手法仍偏向传统吉他摇滚框架内的混合。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — More than a decade after releasing the fairly experimental 'Nocturniquet', The Mars Volta returnedwith a brand-new self-titled studio album, released by Clouds Hill in 2022. A brief hiatus and asecret 2019 reunion led to the formation of an updated lineup featuring the creative core of Omarand Cedric alongside bass player Eva Gardner, drummer Willy Rodriguez and synth player MarcelRodr�guez-L�pez. In what could only be interpreted as a creative reset for the band, 'The MarsVolta' represents a bold and spiritually moving art rock collection that sees the prog innovatorsplaying a warm and melodic combination of danceable Latin rock, neo-psychedelia with electronicundertones, and straightforward indie pop/rock. Undeniably this is the most radio-friendly versionof the band so far, whereas the writing of Omar Rodr�guez-L�pez sounds grounded, smooth, andconfident, and has little in resemblance with the unhinged experimentation that had marked The MarsVolta's earliest efforts.Catchy pop tunes and eerily atmospheric indie ballads prevail here, making this release aninteresting exercise in form and texture from a band known for its exaggerated rock-basedsoundscapes. Gentle Caribbean rhythms and layered ambient sounds provide an almost psychedelicbackdrop to the album, which is quite solid overall. What each musician is playing is clearlyidentifiable, and I find that clarity valuable in an experimentally inclined pop album, although I'mnot convinced that every part of the record works equally well. While you may find extravagant andexciting accessible tunes like 'Blacklight Shine', 'No Case Gain', 'The Requisition', or 'Que DiosTe Maldiga Mi Coraz�n', 'TMV' also features a good amount of watered down and forgettable trackswith an almost complete lack of rhythmic development like 'Cerulea', 'Shore Story', and 'CollapsibleShoulders', that for me add little to no substance to the record and on certain occasions seem to bemere tracklist placeholders. It is this disbalance between excellent and bland that must havestumped most listeners upon hearing this record for the first time, including myself. And while Iappreciate the uncompromising risk the band took with this album, I ultimately have to conclude thatthis is simply not their best work.
items._genre: art rock / neo-psychedelia / Latin rock / indie pop / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张自命名专辑标志着The Mars Volta在沉寂多年后进行的大胆风格转向，从早期极端实验路线回归到更加温度可感的艺术摇滚。 Omar与Cedric的核心创作搭档重组阵容，加入新贝斯手Eva Gardner、鼓手Willy Rodriguez和合成器手Marcel Rodríguez-López，形成更紧凑的乐队编制。专辑将加勒比节奏、迷幻氛围与电子底色融合在朗朗上口的流行摇滚骨架中，Omar的吉他写作变得克制流畅。然而评论指出这种'最电台友好'的尝试存在失衡：'Blacklight Shine''No Case Gain'等曲目兼具可听性与实验质感，但'Cerulea''Shore Story''Collapsible Shoulders'等曲目被指缺乏节奏发展动力，近乎填充。整张专辑在形式与质感上是有趣的实验，但作为Mars Volta作品序列中较为温和的一环，未能达到其前作的高度。

items.body: Review by KansasForEver4 — Five years have passed since CASTANARC's rather mediocre *The Sea of ​​Broken Vows*, which featured eleven tracks ranging from three to five minutes in length?none of them particularly progressive in ambition. This time around, the approach is worlds apart from its predecessor: the album consists of just three tracks, with even the shortest one exceeding the length of the longest song on the 2021 release. One might well call this a "palace revolution"?a genuine surprise, as you can imagine.To appreciate CASTANARC, you first need to like Mark Holiday's somewhat distinctive voice?especially since the album is heavily vocal-driven, though the singing is superb. Yet CASTANARC is also defined by Mark Powell's multifaceted keyboards, which appear all over the album; there is plenty of piano, very little organ, and likely many sounds run through a Mellotron-style filter, with the smooth, fluid synthesizer work serving as the Doncaster band's trademark.We must also mention?lest anyone be overlooked?Neil Duty's excellent guitar work on the second track, "Ceasefire for the Innocent" (Duty previously appeared on the band's 1984 debut, *Journey to the East*, alongside Holiday and Powell); guest musician Dave Holley's contribution is equally impressive on the short "Cue Rain" (though at six minutes, "short" is relative); and the rhythm section?Peter Robinson on bass and Charlie Morgan on drums?delivers a solid, highly competent performance.While it doesn't break the mold with radical originality (remaining firmly within a very conventional neo-progressive vein), it is a fantastic surprise given the band's previous output.
items._cn_summary: 这是CASTANARC乐队暌违五年的专辑，相比前作曲目短小的问题，本次仅以三首长篇作品构成，时长均超过此前最长单曲。主唱Mark Holiday音色独特且演唱出色，键盘手Mark Powell的钢琴、合成器与类Mellotron音色贯穿全片，构成乐队标志；吉他手Neil Duty在第二首中贡献了出色的演奏，嘉宾Dave Holley及贝斯与鼓的节奏组表现稳健。整体制作水准较前作有显著提升，但仍属较为传统的neo-prog范畴，未带来结构或音色上的根本性突破。

items.body: Collage artist Amanda Lee Stilwell of LastCraft Designs and Rosebud Tarot has been reading tarot for over two decades, which is probably long enough to start wondering why the major arcana should have all the fun when an entire generation of musicians spent the 80s dressing as though they had wandered out of an occult manuscript with a synthesizer under one arm. A few years ago, Stilwell began assembling her own artisan deck, filling it with elaborate digital collages drawn from the faces, fashions, poses, and peculiar glamour of New Wave, while borrowing some of the symbolic machinery associated with Pamela Colman Smith’s Rider-Waite illustrations and the Thoth deck. Now, it is currently on display at the Morgan Library’s tarot exhibit in New York City. The resulting New Wave Tarot works because Stilwell clearly knows both sides of the joke. She has done her tarot homework, but she has also paid attention to the people whose records, photographs, haircuts, eyeliner, and stage personas made them such natural candidates for divination in the first place. The suit of Pentacles, or Disks, becomes gold LP records; Swords become microphones; Cups turn into teacups, an affectionate nod to the considerable British presence in the deck; and Wands are represented by eyeliner, which may be one of the few substitutions in tarot history that feels immediately self-explanatory. Then come the casting choices, where the project begins behaving like the record collection of an especially stylish fortune teller. Siouxsie Sioux takes her rightful place as the High Priestess, while Kate Bush presides over the Moon. Fad Gadget, with almost suspicious perfection, appears as the Fool. Robert Smith assumes the King of Cups and returns alongside Mary Poole as the Lovers, a pairing that hardly requires an explanatory pamphlet. Klaus Nomi and David Bowie command the Chariot; Gary Numan becomes the Magician; Budgie and Siouxsie share the Two of Cups. Dave Gahan, Depeche Mode’s dark prince, gets the Devil, while perhaps the smartest piece of casting in the entire deck gives Genesis P-Orridge the card associated with transformation, rupture, passage, and renewal: Death. LastCraft began in 2013 as an outlet for Stilwell’s collage work, pop-cultural fixations, and interest in witchcraft. The company first made its name with an assortment of pop-culture candles, then expanded rapidly as enamel pins, patches, and other witchy accessories joined the catalogue. Stilwell has continued developing her tarot work through projects, including the Rosebud Tarot deck with Diana Rose, which uses found and vintage photography within her recognizable collage approach. The backs of the New Wave Tarot cards carry 80s-inspired geometric designs threaded with roses, giving the deck the look of something that might have fallen out of the sleeve of an obscure 12-inch single bought in 1983 and kept ever since for reasons nobody can adequately explain. Each card measures just under 3 by 5 inches, comes with rounded corners, and is printed on premium thick card stock. The complete deck ships in a tuck box with a fold-out guide explaining the cards and offering instructions for readers who would like to consult your higher self with this wonderfully strange congregation. Your order comes shipped in a tuck box that holds the entire deck and a fold-out description of cards and details on how to read the deck. This order is a preorder. They anticipate shipping out decks by the end of October 2026. NOTE: This will be the final printing of the New Wave Tarot, which has been out of print for several years and revived due to high demand. The deck is available for pre-sale ONLY here. They hope to reach 150 orders minimum. Music fans, dabblers in the occult, you know what to do. Let the spirits move you. Major Arcana cards include: Gary Numan Siouxsie Sioux Nina Hagen Peter Murphy Nick Cave Robert Smith/Mary Poole Klaus Nomi/David Bowie Frank Tovey Andrew Eldritch Devo Grace Jones Ian Curtis Gen P-Orridge Morrissey Dave Gahan Kate Bush Marc Almond Pete Burns Photo: Alice Teeple Model: Frankie Starker The post New Wave Tarot Deals a Final Hand with Siouxsie Sioux, Dave Gahan, Robert Smith, and More! appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非传统意义上的乐评，而是介绍艺术家Amanda Lee Stilwell创作的"New Wave Tarot"塔罗牌作品。该项目将80年代新浪潮与后朋克音乐人的形象融入传统韦特塔罗牌结构中：权杖以眼线笔呈现，宝剑化作麦克风，五芒星变为金色黑胶唱片。选角方面颇具巧思——Siouxsie Sioux对应女祭司，Kate Bush对应月亮，Fad Gadget对应愚者，Robert Smith与Mary Poole对应恋人，Genesis P-Orridge对应死神（暗示变革与重生）。作品在视觉层面将塔罗符号学与新浪潮的时尚美学相融合，现于纽约Morgan图书馆塔罗展览中展出。文章本身更像文化新闻报道而非深度乐评，涉及的音乐人虽涵盖暗潮与后朋克范畴，但核心内容围绕艺术装置而非音乐本体展开。

items.body: Los Angeles duo Patriarchy released an official video for “Lilylicker” on 29 September 2026. The track is the second song on the EP “Appendices,” released 7 August 2026 as a companion to the band’s 2025 album “Manual for Dying.” Appendices by Patriarchy The track opens on a low synth line and a steady kick drum, with Huizenga’s vocals half-whispered through the verses. The arrangement hardens into an industrial-techno beat partway through, with distorted guitars entering on the chorus. Patriarchy describes its own sound as “snuff pop,” a mix of metal, synthpop, punk and dance music. “Appendices” runs five tracks: “Bite Marks,” “Lilylicker,” “Servile,” “Ode (to an Apprehensive Tyrant)” and “Hate Fuck.” Huizenga and English wrote, performed, produced and recorded all five themselves. AJ English mixed “Lilylicker” and Enyang Urbiks mastered it. Witch Club Satan adds backing vocals on “Servile.” The EP is also out as a limited 12-inch clear vinyl edition of 300 copies, shipping around 1 November 2026, alongside digital formats on Bandcamp and streaming services. Patriarchy’s video for ‘Lilylicker’ Patriarchy directed the “Lilylicker” video itself, with cinematography by Hazel Hill McCarthy. Huizenga appears in a white gown holding lilies, then in a pink dress with chains and a metallic corset with gold wings; AJ English, also known as The Drummer, holds a skull and wears white wings. Huizenga’s son also appears in the video. The crew had to relocate the shoot outdoors to the hills above Los Angeles after the original studio balked at the concept and at having a child on set. Huizenga said the move improved the result: “A lot of the things that went ‘wrong’ ultimately added to the beauty of it, like having to shoot outside, where moths kept flying in front of our lenses.” On the project’s name and intent, Huizenga commented: “Patriarchy has never been about perfection, it’s about realizing we are the last remnants of human existence before AI enslaves us all; that’s why the project is called Patriarchy after all.” About Patriarchy Patriarchy formed in Los Angeles as a collaboration between Actually Huizenga and Andrew Means, who met when his band 3TEETH played a show at Das Bunker and offered to work with her in the studio between tour dates. Huizenga had been focused on filmmaking after a prior solo album, “Predator Romantic,” but the sessions with Means led the two to release the songs and build a band around them. Patriarchy released its debut album, “Asking for It,” on 8 November 2019 through Dero Arcade. The band built on that start with “The Unself,” released 26 August 2022, and “Manual for Dying,” out 19 September 2025 and trailed by the singles “Boy on a Leash,” “New Way” and “Die Like Everyone Else.” Patriarchy’s current lineup pairs Huizenga with AJ English, known as The Drummer. The band’s videos, including the earlier live performance clip “No Touch Torture,” are staged and directed largely by Huizenga herself. “Appendices,” the band’s companion EP to “Manual for Dying,” draws on Oscar Wilde, the Marchesa Luisa Casati, the emperor Tiberius and the Manson family as reference points. “Lilylicker” is the second single pulled from that EP, following “Servile,” and its video is Patriarchy’s newest visual release.
items._cn_summary: Patriarchy 是来自洛杉矶的双人组合，自称"snuff pop"，将金属、合成器流行、朋克与舞曲融合。《Appendices》是其2025年专辑《Manual for Dying》的配套EP，共五首曲目，由两人独立完成词曲、演奏、录制与制作。《Lilylicker》以低频合成器线条与稳定底鼓开场，人声半低语般穿过主歌，中段编排硬化为工业techno节拍，副歌处引入失真吉他。MV由乐队自导，Huizenga身着白裙手持百合、金翼金属胸衣等造型出镜，AJ English持骷髅头出现，拍摄因原工作室拒绝方案而转至洛杉矶郊外山区完成。项目名称源自对AI议题的回应，暗含对父权制与技术统治的批判。整体呈现暗潮与工业电子的混合质感，视觉风格强烈，但音乐上的实验深度有限。

items.body: Canadian electronic duo Delerium release their 16th studio album, “Exaudire”, on 22 January 2027 via Metropolis Records. The album arrives on regular CD and as a limited edition double vinyl pressed on oxblood-colored vinyl in a deluxe gatefold sleeve. The title “Exaudire” is Latin for listening, hearing and being heard. Metropolis Records describes the album as moving between the tangible and the dreamlike, built from electronic textures, expansive atmospheres and guest vocal performances. Side-Line previously reported on the album’s lead single, Into the Light, which embeds portions of Diamanda Galás’s 1986 recording “Deliver Me from Mine Enemies: IV. Ε Ξελόυ Mε (Deliver Me)” from her album “The Divine Punishment”. Exaudire by Delerium ‘Exaudire’ tracklist and guest vocalists The 12-track “Exaudire” features five different guest vocalists across its running order, confirmed via the album’s Bandcamp listing: “Higher Power” (feat. Mimi Page), “Into the Light” (feat. Diamanda Galás), “Dream Palace” (feat. Magic Wands), “Buried Light” (feat. Mimi Page), “Apocalypse” (feat. Inna Walters), “Stolen” (feat. Phildel), “Into the Unknown” (feat. Jaël), “Multiplying Zero” (feat. Inna Walters), “Chasing the Wind” (feat. Mimi Page), “Exaudire”, “Had to Go” (feat. Jaël) and “Litany” (feat. Mimi Page). Mimi Page is an American singer-songwriter and composer who has released four full-length albums since 2011. Magic Wands, a dream pop trio from Los Angeles, are also signed to Metropolis Records, with the albums “Switch” (2023) and “Cascades” (2025). Jaël, a Swiss singer, previously collaborated with Delerium on the 2003 EP “After All” and the album “Chimera”. Inna Walters, based in Nashville, already appeared on Delerium’s 2023 album “Signs”. Phildel is a classically trained English singer, pianist and songwriter from London. Delerium songs have previously appeared in the films “Brokedown Palace” and “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider”. “Silence”, the duo’s 2000 collaboration with Sarah McLachlan, was more recently heard in the BBC drama “Industry”. Side-Line also covered Peter Murphy and Boy George’s 2026 Delerium remix of “Let the Flowers Grow” and Restless Mosaic’s tribute track referencing the project. About Delerium Delerium was founded in Vancouver, Canada, in 1987 by Bill Leeb and original collaborator Michael Balch. Rhys Fulber later joined as Leeb’s main songwriting partner. Both Leeb and Fulber built their reputation in the electro-industrial group Front Line Assembly, and Delerium initially served as an outlet for dark, cinematic ambient soundscapes distinct from that project’s harder industrial sound. Early albums “Faces, Forms & Illusions” and “Morpheus” appeared in 1989. Through the 1990s, Delerium’s sound evolved from industrial electronics and ambient trance toward song-based electronic pop built around guest vocalists, a shift marked by 1994’s “Semantic Spaces”, which introduced a rotating cast of female singers on largely downtempo songs, a format the duo has used on every album since. “Karma” (1997) established Delerium’s more danceable side, and “Poem” (2000), produced with Chris Peterson, included “Silence” featuring Sarah McLachlan, which reached worldwide chart success and won a Juno Award in 2000. After the Leeb-Fulber reunion album “Chimera” (2003), Delerium continued through “Nuages du Monde” (2006), “Music Box Opera” (2012), the atmospheric “Mythologie” (2016) and “Signs” (2023), the latter featuring Inna Walters among other vocalists. “Exaudire” is Delerium’s 16th studio album and its first collaboration with Diamanda Galás.
items._cn_summary: 加拿大电子双人组Delerium即将发行第十六张录音室专辑《Exaudire》，拉丁语含义为倾听、被听见。专辑在电子质感与氛围铺陈之间游走，并邀请五位客座歌手参与录制，包括Diamanda Galás、Mimi Page、Magic Wands、Inna Walters、Jaël与Phildel。首支单曲《Into the Light》取样了Diamanda Galás 1986年的录音片段，将工业人声与电子氛围编织在一起。专辑由独立厂牌Metropolis Records发行，提供CD与限量牛血色双黑胶版本。乐评以新闻通稿形式罗列曲目与艺人背景，缺乏对音乐本体深入分析与个人审美判断。

items.body: De/Vision, the German synth-pop duo of Steffen Keth and Thomas Adam, released their sixth studio album “Two” on 1 October 2001 through E-Wave Records, a division of Drakkar Entertainment GmbH distributed by BMG. The De/Vision “Two” album turns 25 this year. It was the first De/Vision studio album recorded as a duo, following Markus Ganssert’s departure from the band in 2000. De/Vision ‘Two’ tracklist and credits The ten-track CD runs “All I Ever Do,” “Silent Moan,” “Drowning Soul,” “Heroine,” “Blindness,” “Heart-Shaped Tumor,” “State of Mind,” “Escape the World,” “Uncaring Machine” and “Lonely Day.” Georg Kaleve produced and mixed the album, with Keth handling pre-production; Stefan Ulrich engineered the sessions, recorded across Pizza Hat and Mikrokosmos-Studio in Berlin and Palais Aux Etoiles in Bremen, and Michael Schwabe mastered the record at Skyline Tonfabrik in Düsseldorf. Achim Färber played drums, Josef Bach added piano, and Kaleve, Bach and Lars Baumgardt contributed guitar; vocalist Sandrine appears on “State of Mind” and Clara Hill supplies additional vocals elsewhere on the album. Dirk Rudolph designed the sleeve around cover photography by Christof Schulte and band photography by Harald Hoffmann. “Two” peaked at number 42 on the German album chart. Lead single “Heart-Shaped Tumor” reached number 89 in Germany that September, De/Vision’s first charting single since “We Fly… Tonight” in 1998. A Different Drum issued a separate US edition of the album in 2004, and Popgefahr Records released a 17-track deluxe reissue of “Two” in 2016, adding instrumental and remix material to the original ten songs. About De/Vision De/Vision formed in July 1988 in Bensheim, near Darmstadt, Germany, as a quartet of Steffen Keth, Thomas Adam, Markus Ganssert and Stefan Blender. Blender left in 1991. The band self-released the single “Your Hands on My Skin” in 1990 and issued “Boy on the Street” in 1992 through Synthetic Product Records, before the 1993 maxi single “Try to Forget” brought them to Strange Ways Records. The debut album “World Without End” followed in January 1994, and “Unversed in Love” arrived in January 1995, both on Strange Ways. “Fairyland?” followed in August 1996 and became the band’s first German chart entry, and “Monosex” moved the band to WEA Records in 1998, reaching number 30. Ganssert left the group in 2000, the same year “Void” reached number 34 on WEA. Keth and Adam, now a duo, signed to E-Wave Records for “Two,” released on 1 October 2001 and distributed internationally through BMG. The duo continued on E-Wave through “Devolution” (2003), “6 Feet Underground” (2004), “Subkutan” (2006) and “NOOB” (2007), before founding their own label, Popgefahr Records, in 2009. Later albums “Popgefahr” (2010), “Rockets and Swords” (2012), “13” (2016) and “Citybeats” (2018) all appeared on Popgefahr, alongside the 2016 deluxe reissue of “Two.” Keth also records with Daniel Myer of Haujobb as Devision Redux, and De/Vision themselves toured with Lakeside X and Empathy Test in 2025. Twenty-five years on, “Two” marks the album that opened the Keth/Adam duo era of the band.
items._cn_summary: 本文为德国合成器流行二人组De/Vision第六张录音室专辑《Two》25周年纪念性回顾文章。专辑2001年由E-Wave Records发行，是乐队成员Ganssert离队后首张以二人组形式录制完成的唱片。Georg Kaleve担任制作与混音，Keth负责前期制作，录音分别在柏林和不来梅的多家工作室完成。十首曲目由词曲创作者Adam与Keth主导，鼓手Färber、钢琴手Bach与吉他手Baumgardt等客座乐手参与录制。专辑在德国专辑榜最高排名第42位，主打单曲《Heart-Shaped Tumor》成为乐队1998年以来首支打入榜单的作品。2004年A Different Drum发行美国版，2016年Popgefahr推出17曲豪华再版，补充器乐与混音素材。文章以事实性信息梳理为主，缺乏对音乐风格、制作手法或艺术价值的深度评论。
